","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"New Council meeting management system
The Shire has recently implemented a new Council meeting management system, provided by Redman Solutions.
For members of the public, this means the way you access agendas, minutes and livestreams for Council and Committee meetings on the Shire’s website may look a little different.
We’ve made these changes to provide a more user-friendly and streamlined experience. To help you navigate the new system, we’ve included helpful information on the Shire’s website.
We’re confident this upgrade will make it easier for you to stay informed and engaged with Council decisions.

Switched On Business Award to Wasteless Pantry Mundaring 
Congratulations to Mundaring’s Wasteless Pantry who recently received a Switched On Business Award through the Switch Your Thinking Program, recognising its outstanding commitment to sustainability.
Since 2015, the Wasteless Pantry has helped the community reduce waste through refillable products, education and food rescue efforts.
Congratulations once again to Wasteless Pantry Mundaring on this well-deserved recognition.

40 years of the Katharine Susannah Prichard Writers Centre
Congratulations to the Katharine Susannah Prichard Writers Centre, Greenmount, which recently celebrated 40 years since its inaugural meeting in 1985.
This milestone was marked with a heartwarming afternoon tea, recognising the centre’s rich history and exciting future. As part of the celebrations, six talented writers, supported through the 2025 KSP Literary Development Awards, were also acknowledged.
Since its beginnings, the KSP Writers Centre has grown into a dynamic hub for creativity, mentorship and artistic exchange.
Congratulations once again to the KSP Writers Centre team on this significant achievement and for all they continue to do for the community.

New Citizens
Last week, the Shire welcomed 54 new Australian citizens at a special citizenship ceremony, officiated by Deputy Shire President Cr Luke Ellery. 
These individuals and families have chosen to call our Shire home, and they represent a diverse group with backgrounds spanning more than 20 countries – including the United Kingdom, Germany, South Africa, India, Thailand and many others.
On behalf of Council, I extend our congratulations and a sincere welcome to all our new citizens.

Summary of Questions
Summary of Response
Christian Jackson-Stegner - Chidlow
1Can the Shire of Mundaring, CEO Council or President or the officers communicate with the state level about future development areas inside the Shire and influence what kind of property sizes will be planned by all developers?
The Chief Executive Officer advised that Council is currently going through a process of reviewing its Local Planning Strategy and also its Local Planning Scheme. These are the two instruments that Council would use in the context of the state planning framework to influence issues.
2Can Shire of Mundaring CEO, officers and the Council influence future development areas in regards to property size fitting better to the Perth hills lifestyle?
The Chief Executive Officer advised the response would be the same as the previous question, that the Shire is undertaking that review at the moment to review zonings and land usage.

RESOLUTION NUMBER:C-6-7-2025 
ALTERNATIVE MOTION / COUNCIL DECISION    
Moved by:Cr Zlatnik
Seconded by:Cr Cicchini

That Council:

  1. Submits a request to Department of Planning, Land and Heritage to excise a portion of the ‘Public Recreation’ reserve to enter into a direct lease or provide provisions for power to lease/licence in a new management order to be held by the Shire;

  2. Acknowledges that a detailed site survey will be conducted prior to the submission of this request, to determine the exact area to be excised to ensure optimal land use and public amenity (through the inclusion of vegetation buffers, suitable allowances for parking, delivery truck access and pedestrian friendly accessways and development of commercial building space); and

  3. Subject to the Department of Planning, Land and Heritage decision pursuant to resolution 1, Shire Officers prepare the necessary LPS4 Amendment documentation for Council’s consideration.
CARRIED 6/1
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Zlatnik, Cr Ellery, Cr Beale, Cr Cicchini
Against:Cr Jeans

Reason for the Change
To provide greater clarity and transparency on the intent of the request to excise and rezone a portion of Lot 8939 Ellesmere Road, Swan View; ensuring that it enables the appropriate development of Lot 8939 Ellesmere Road to meet community needs, now and into the future, as well as improving community amenity through the inclusion of improved, functional public open space and commercial spaces.

The Shire of Mundaring Recreation Facilities Strategy 2025 (Attachment 1) be endorsed with the following amendments:

Our Guiding Principles - Reword the following two principles

  • Access for All: Ensuring every resident, as far as practicable, has equitable access to sport and recreation facilities.
  • Sustainable by Design: Championing environmentally sustainable design practices to reduce our carbon footprint and minimise water and energy usage.

Against:Cr Cicchini

Summary of Questions
Summary of Response
Tom Johns - Mundaring Ratepayers Progress Association (MRRA)
1Can the entry and exit to Shire of Mundaring Admin Building customer carpark be addressed for safety reasons, and that it gets put into the budget as a priority.The Chief Executive Officer advised there is no funding allocated in the current budget, nor is there any related item in the Council Plan. The Shire can engage with MRRA to better understand the concerns and consider a position. Alternatively, MRRA may raise the matter with a Councillor, who could submit a notice of motion. The Shire President further advised that a motion could also be moved at an Annual Electors meeting.
2Is anything being done to address the traffic issues experienced in the centre of Mundaring around the shopping centres?The Chief Executive Officer advised there are no specific plans relating to the shopping centres. The Shire is considering traffic flow on the opposite side of the highway as part of the town centre revitalisation. While intersections such as Stoneville Road (at the shopping centre exit) are being monitored, no comprehensive study is currently underway.

ALTERNATIVE MOTION
Moved by:Cr Ellery
Seconded by:Cr Mehta
That Council, by absolute majority, adopts:

1. The following waste charges for the collection and disposal of waste in accordance with the provisions of the Waste Avoidance & Resources Recovery Act 2007:
  1. For residential properties with a bin collection service, a rubbish and waste service charge of $550.
  2. For residential properties with a 240L General Waste Bin swapped out in place of a 140L General Waste Bin, a charge of $105.
  3. For multi-unit residential properties with a shared bin collection service, a rubbish and waste service charge of $465.
  4. For non-rateable properties with a FOGO and General Waste Collection service, a rubbish and waste charge of $354.
  5. For non-rateable properties with a kerbside recycling, a charge of $95. 
  6. For non-rateable properties with a transfer station pass, a charge of $220.
  7. Any additional 140L General Waste Bin services, a charge of $130 per service.
  8. Any additional 240L General Waste Bin services, a charge of $235 per service.
  9. Any additional Recycling Bin services, a charge of $75 per service.  
  10. Any additional FOGO Bin services, a charge of $175 per service. 
  11. For commercial properties, a charge of $265 for a General Waste Bin serviced once a week.
  12. For commercial properties, a charge of $95 for a kerbside recycling service of once per fortnight.
  13. For commercial properties, a charge of $195 for a weekly FOGO collection service.
  14. For commercial properties, a charge of $1400 for a weekly bulk General Waste bin service (660 litres); and
  15. For commercial properties, a charge of $1200 for each additional lift for a weekly bulk General Waste bin service (660 litres); and
2.  The Annual Budget for the year ending 30 June 2026 as detailed in Attachment 1, incorporating but not limited to the following:
a) A general rate of 9.20012 cents in the dollar of the Gross Rental Value to be levied on all rateable property within the Shire of Mundaring for the      2025/26 financial year. 
b) A general rate of 0.67058 cents in the dollar to be levied on all Unimproved Value property within the Shire of Mundaring for the 2025/26 financial year.
c) A minimum rate of $1019 for the 2025/26 financial year for Gross Rental Value Properties. 
d) A minimum rate of $1288 for the 2025/26 financial year for Unimproved Value Properties. 
e) The following dates being set for payment of rates by instalments and payment in full be approved:                          
    i) Full payment or First instalment due date of 19 September 2025 or 35 days after the date of issue appearing on the rates notice, whichever is the later.
    ii) Second instalment due date of 21 November 2025 or two months after the due date of the first instalment, whichever is the later.
    iii) Third instalment due date of 23 January 2026 or two months after the due date of the second instalment, whichever is the later. 
    iv) Fourth and final instalment due date of 27 March 2026 or two months after the due date of the third instalment, whichever is the later.
f) An interest rate of 7% per annum payable on rates, or any instalment of a rates, that remains unpaid after it is due and payable. 
g) An interest rate of 11% per annum payable on the ESL charge, or any instalment of the ESL charge, that remains unpaid after it is due and payable. 
h) The interest rate of 7% per annum is not applied to unpaid rates for eligible pensioners, eligible seniors and deceased estates subject to probate.
i) The maintaining of an overdraft facility of up to $500,000 and credit card facility of up to $56,000 for the purpose of providing a credit facility for normal Municipal Fund operational expenditure during the year. 
j) The adoption of the following Elected Members Fees and Allowances for 2025/26:
       i) An annual allowance in lieu of meeting fees for elected members other than the Shire President of $26,020. 
       ii) An annual allowance in lieu of meeting fees for the Shire President of $34,890. 
       iii) An annual allowance for the Shire President of $70,951. 
       iv) An annual allowance for the Deputy Shire President of $17,738; and 
       v) An Information and Communication Technology Allowance of $3500 per Elected Member. 
k) The 2025/26 capital works program as detailed in the budget. 
l) The Schedule of Fees and Charges for the 2025/26 as detailed in the budget noting the change for rubbish and waste service charge for residential to $550 and multi-unit residential to $465
m) An additional general waste collection be trailed and undertaken to all residential and multi-unit residential properties in the Christmas / New Year period with information on tonnages, contamination and community feedback to inform future budgets.

3. The budget be amended to include a transfer from the Waste Reserve of $412,670 to fund the reduction in waste charges and income. 

Reason for the change
To manage the waste increase for households due to increased tonnages whilst allowing prudent reserves to manage future Waste improvements. The Additional General waste collection trial supports households to manage waste during a busy period and reduce contamination of FOGO/Recycling that may result in tonnes being sent to landfill.

MOTION 
Moved by:Cr Daw
Seconded by:Cr Zlatnik
That Council:
 1. Opposes any proposed expansion of the ALCOA exploration and mining operations into the Mundaring Weir Catchment and Northern Jarrah Forest because of the severe damage to the environment and loss of habitat for local native species that would result from clearing access for exploration and potential future mining operations.
 2. Writes a submission to the EPA prior to 21 August 2025, expressing the Shire's opposition to the proposal to expand exploration and mining activities on the grounds that such activity pose significant environmental and sustainability impacts, through:
  • loss of biodiversity values of the Northern Jarrah Forest;
  • inadequacy of rehabilitation;
  • risks to water quality and quantity;
  • risk to the spread of dieback (phytophthora cinnamoni)
  • risk to increased salinity
  • reduction in recreation, tourism and amenity values, opportunities and community access; and
  • risk to the long-term character, public health and amenity of the Perth Hills region
 3. Requests the Shire President to engage with neighbouring Local Government Mayors/Presidents to explore opportunities for a regional advocacy position.


RESOLUTION NUMBER:C-5-8-2025 
AMENDMENT / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Pres McNeil
Seconded by:Cr Mehta
4. Request the Shire President to write to ALCOA requesting the voluntary excise of the Mundaring Weir Catchment area from the proposed exploration drilling program contained within Mining Management Plan 2023-27 and Mineral Lease 1SA and that reference to the letter be included in the Shire's formal submission to the Environmental Protection Authority.
CARRIED 7/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Jeans, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Zlatnik, Cr Ellery, Cr Cicchini
Against:None

RESOLUTION NUMBER:C-6-8-2025 
MOTION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Daw
Seconded by:Cr Zlatnik
That Council:
 1. Strongly opposes any proposed expansion of the ALCOA exploration and mining operations into the Mundaring Weir Catchment and Northern Jarrah Forest because of the severe damage to the environment and loss of habitat for local native species that would result from clearing access for exploration and potential future mining operations.
 2. Writes a submission to the EPA prior to 21 August 2025, expressing the Shire's opposition to the proposal to expand exploration and mining activities on the grounds that such activity pose significant environmental and sustainability impacts, through:
  • loss of biodiversity values of the Northern Jarrah Forest;
  • inadequacy of rehabilitation;
  • risks to water quality and quantity;
  • risk to the spread of dieback (phytophthora cinnamoni)
  • risk to increased salinity
  • reduction in recreation, tourism and amenity values, opportunities and community access; and
  • risk to the long-term character, public health and amenity of the Perth Hills region
 3. Requests the Shire President to engage with neighbouring Local Government Mayors/Presidents to explore opportunities for a regional advocacy position.
4. Request the Shire President to write to ALCOA requesting the voluntary excise of the Mundaring Weir Catchment area from the proposed exploration drilling program contained within Mining Management Plan 2023-27 and Mineral Lease 1SA and that reference to the letter be included in the Shire’s formal submission to the Environmental Protection Authority.
CARRIED 7/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Jeans, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Zlatnik, Cr Ellery, Cr Cicchini
Against:None

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"2025 Swan Chamber of Commerce Business Awards
On Saturday, the Swan Chamber of Commerce hosted its 2025 Business Awards. Shire of Mundaring, along with the Mundaring Chamber of Commerce, was proud to be a Gold Sponsor, acknowledging outstanding local talent and service within our business community.
Special congratulations to:
  • Amaroo Retreat, winner of the Hospitality Award, for delivering outstanding service and unforgettable customer experiences.
  • Snap Print Solutions Midland, a proud Sawyers Valley local owner, winner of the Service Excellence Award, for going above and beyond in every interaction.
  • Rebecca De Vries Photography, winner of the Arts and Design Award, recognising talent that defies the boundaries of creativity.
We also congratulate all finalists and winners. These achievements reflect the strength and spirit of our local businesses, and we couldn’t be prouder.

Youth Travel Grants
Shire of Mundaring is proud to support the achievements of our young people through the Youth Travel Grant program. This funding assists with travel costs for events across sport and recreation, science and technology, the arts, community service, culture, and the environment.
This round, we congratulate:
  • Aaden Kettle, representing Western Australia at the Australian School Sport Swimming Championships in Brisbane.
  • Emily Anderson, competing in the XTERRA World Championship Sprint Triathlon in Italy.
  • Willow Burr, competing in the World Skate Oceania and Pacific Cup Artistic Championship in Queensland.

Summary of Questions
Summary of Response
Christian Jackson Stegner - Chidlow
1What kind of higher level,  state or federal government,  can and will the Shire reach out to to bring forward the outcome of today's Council decision of topic 11.2 expansion of Alcoa mining proposal when the motion would be passed?
The Shire President advised that the motion would need to first be passed before reaching out to representatives of the State Government.
The Chief Executive Officer also advised that it would be pre-emptive to provide any more advice given the matter is currently before Council.  Once Council has made a determination, depending on the outcome of the determination, the Shire President and CEO would work out what advocacy is required and which state ministers.


2What kind of legal actions, in any form, that could be in a letter or could there be any further action to talk to ministers and any kind of levels in state or federal government?The Shire President advised that depending on the outcome of the motion then the level of advocacy will be determined.
The Chief Éxecutive Officer also advised that depending on the outcome in accordance with the Notice of Motion, then the Shire would make a submission to the EPA given that there is potential for drilling that could occur within our Shire.  The Shire would make a submission under a public environmental review.  That would be the Shire's first step. 
John Bell - Mt Helena
1Will Council consider establishing a policy when meetings will be closed to the public?The Shire President advised that there are a number of reasons why meetings are closed to the public, including the Local Government Act and Regulations and also the Shire of Mundaring Meeting Procedure Local Law.
The Chief Executive Officer also advised that the Local Government Act covers when Council can go behind closed doors and that is further expanded in the Shire's Meeting Procedure Local Law. When the Shire receives an item it is the CEO's responsibility to advise Council what the most appropriate course of action is.  That includes what reference the Act makes or to determine whether there's anything that could be from a legislative point of view that would require Council to go behind closed doors with respect to the item.  The reason going behind closed doors for Item 13.4 on tonight's agenda is that the Shire has received legal advice so that is the purpose of going behind closed doors.
2Regarding the forthcoming elections, will Council consider establishing a political interest register?The Shire President advised there are different ways this can be bought to Council.  Elected Members can bring up as Notice of Motion.  It could also be raised as a motion for Council to consider at the Annual Electors' meeting.  With local government elections coming up, the easiest way is for the community to ask candidates directly if they're aligned.
The Chief Executive Officer advised he is happy to provide a more detailed response, however, his first sense would be that it could be beyond the Shire's power to actually require that information to be disclosed by potential candidates, given that Council's are governed by not only the Local Government Act but also during elections, the WA Electoral Commission.  Therefore Council may not have the power to compel candidates to disclose that information.

That Council receives the consultant's report and endorses the following:

  1. Notes the Salaries and Allowances Tribunal Determination of 4th April 2025 (effective 1st July 2025). 
  2. Notes an increase in the Superannuation Guarantee Levy from 11.5% to 12% effective 1st July 2025. 
  3. Notes the outcomes of the Elected Member Performance Survey undertaken in July 2025 with the Chief Executive Officer being assessed at ‘Meets Expectations’ in this year’s performance appraisal. 
  4. Adopt the modified performance criteria metrics for the 2025-2026 performance period outlined in Section 7.6 of this confidential report.

  8. Comply, as per Division 3 of the Local Government (Administration) Regulations Schedule 2 clause 19, by notifying the Chief Executive Officer of results of this performance review.
CARRIED 7/0

Moved by:Pres McNeil

That Council;

  1. Endorse the Concept Design for the Mundaring Cultural Hub Project, including the proposed Schedule of Accommodation for the community usage spaces and other user groups.
  2. Endorse the financial not-to exceed value of the full Mundaring Cultural Hub Project at $35 million.
  3. Notes the Concept Design for the Mundaring Cultural Hub Project excludes the Toy Library and Child Health Clinic from further design development.
  4. Approve amalgamation of the three lots – 3165, 3185 and 3205 Jacoby Street, Mundaring, forming the consolidated land parcel required to allow the Western Power application for the power supply of the Mundaring Cultural Hub Project to proceed.
  5. Formally acknowledge the receipt of the $15 million Thriving Suburbs grant from the Federal Government for the Mundaring Cultural Hub Project.

RESOLUTION NUMBER: SC-3-09-2025
MOTION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Pres McNeil
Seconded by:Cr Zlatnik
That Council:
  1. Receives the Concept Design for the Mundaring Cultural Hub Project, including the proposed Schedule of Accommodation for the community usage spaces and other user groups;
  2. Requests the Mundaring Cultural Hub Concept Design, Schedule of Accommodation, Operational Management Model and Risk Assessment be presented to Council at a future forum, for Council to provide additional feedback, prior to consideration at a future Council meeting with the following parameters;
    1. The financial not-to exceed value of the full Mundaring Cultural Hub Project at $32 million;
    2. A minimum of two Mundaring Cultural Hub alternative elevations be provided for Council to consider; and
    3. Future Concept Designs for the Mundaring Cultural Hub Project to exclude the Toy Library and Child Health Clinic; 
  3. Approve amalgamation of the three lots – 3165, 3185 and 3205 Jacoby Street, Mundaring, forming the consolidated land parcel required to allow the Western Power application for the power supply of the Mundaring Cultural Hub Project to proceed; and
  4. Formally acknowledge the receipt of the $15 million Thriving Suburbs grant from the Federal Government for the Mundaring Cultural Hub Project.
CARRIED 8/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Jeans, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Zlatnik, Cr Ellery, Cr Beale, Cr Cicchini
Against:None

Reason for the Change: 
The proposed $35m cost is beyond the comfort levels of Council given current phase of project design is at Concept Level which represents a cost accuracy of around +30% to -15%. It is also important to note that while the budget has increased from $22m, the net cost to Council has decreased due to the Thriving Suburbs grant with Council originally underwriting the project with $10m in debt finance which is no longer being proposed. Council would like to give the concept more consideration at a future forum prior to a final endorsement to proceed to detailed design and tendering.

RESOLUTION NUMBER:SC-4-9-2025 
MOTION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Jeans
Seconded by:Cr Cicchini
That the order of business be changed as follows:

  • Item 6.1.4 be considered prior to Item 6.1.1.

CARRIED 8/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Jeans, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Zlatnik, Cr Ellery, Cr Beale, Cr Cicchini
Against:None

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Still time to sign up for E-rates to win!
There’s still time to sign up for eRates and go into the draw to win up to four thousand dollars off your rates. Everyone who subscribes before Thursday 18 September is in the running to win a full credit on their 2024/25 rates and rubbish charges. It only takes a couple of minutes to sign up on the Shire’s website.

Local Government Elections
Nominations for the Local Government Elections have now closed. Candidate details are available on the Shire’s website. There won't be an election in South Ward as the number of nominations received matched the number of vacancies. Postal voting packages will be delivered soon. Please make sure your vote is received by six o’clock on 18 October. If you don’t think you can return it by post in time, you can hand-deliver it to the Shire Administration Building during business hours, or between 8am and 6pm on polling day.

New website is launching soon 
I’m pleased to share that Shire of Mundaring will launch its new website this Wednesday, 10 September. The upgrade will make it much easier for our community to find information, pay bills, see what’s on, and access services online. The new look, clearer menus and improved search engine mean you’ll be able to get things done faster and with less hassle. From Wednesday, I encourage you to jump on to explore the new site.
 
TARMAC West – Parkerville rally 19 September
The Lance East Exotics Tarmac West rally is coming to Perth and surrounds from Thursday 18 to Sunday 21 September. Drivers will race the clock over 250 kilometres of closed roads — from fast, flowing sections to tight, technical stages. You can catch the action in Parkerville on McDowell Loop on Friday 19 September. For details, visit the Tarmac West website

WanderFest – Lake Leschenaultia
Finally, Lake Leschenaultia will be part of the Perth Hills WanderFest later this month. From Friday 26 to Monday 29 September, you can join guided hikes around the lake, with start times varying each day. There’ll also be free, family-friendly events on Saturday the 27th and Sunday the 28th from 10am to 2pm. Summary of QuestionsSummary of Response
Eric Smith - Glen Forrest
1Now that Old York Road has been resurfaced, will new bus shelters replace the damaged ones?This question was taken on notice.
2Regarding the recent verge side collection throughout the Shire, how much does this contract cost and can the clean-up be done in a better way?Director Built and Natural Environment advised the current contract is based on per tonne collected, therefore, until the works have been completed the final cost is unknown. In previous years, the cost has generally been around $500,000 which includes the cost of disposal. 

Council has tasked Shire officers to prepare a report regarding a booking system instead of the current annual verge side collection, and this will be presented to Council in due course.
Carolyn Baldwin - Parkerville
1What are the exact setback regulations which apply to the unauthorised building currently being completed in a stable on our fence line (stable address is 2165 Gill Street)?Director Place and Community advised development requirements under the Shire’s Local Planning Scheme No. 4 state that any proposed structure on a Rural Residential site requires a minimum setback of 10 metres to the lot boundary. Please be advised that the existing stable pre-dates the requirements of the scheme, hence why the current structure is approved with the located on the boundary.
2What is the exact internal floor space in square metres of the unauthorised building currently being completed as an ancillary dwelling on our fence line at 2165 Gill Street?Director Place and Community advised the Shire’s database suggests that the existing stable on the site at 2165 Gill Street is approximately 195m2 in area. It is advised that ongoing compliance investigations are being had regarding its potential conversion, and Shire officers are continuing to assess an appropriate way forward with any future decision making on the matter. 
Alan Baldwin - Parkerville
1Is a property owner who shares a fence line with my property allowed to construct an unauthorised ancillary dwelling on my fence line without:
  • Planning approval
  • Building permit
  • Notice of completion
  • BAL rating in an extreme fire area
  • Bushfire management statement 
Director Place and Community advised ancillary dwellings require appropriate approvals including planning and building approvals. Where the appropriate approvals are not in place, the Shire will advise the landowner of the requirements to achieve compliance and rectify any issues, noting if compliance cannot be achieved, then other avenues are then pursued. 

Planning applications require relevant BAL approvals as part of any development approval process. The property falls under the Shire’s Bushfire Special Control Area of Local Planning Scheme 4 and is mapped as Extreme. A BAL would therefore be required as part of any future application for development approval.
2If Shire officers are made aware of and inspect a non-approved construction and can clearly see there is no way the construction will be able to comply e.g. size, location, setbacks, BAL rating etc, why wouldn't the Shire issue an immediate stop work order until the investigations are complete?Director Place and Community advised the approach being taken by Shire officers is to highlight the non-compliance matters and advise the proponent of the approvals they would require, and the process they need to follow to rectify. 

In relation to any stop work order, the Shire is not proposing to lodge anything official at this time as any works which might be undertaken in the short term are internal and not considered to be a works which, amongst other things, pose a risk to human life or the environment, or contribute to immediate amenity issues which would have an impact on neighbours. The Shire is working to progress this matter to ensure compliance.
Eric Smith - Glen Forrest
3Current verge collection and clean up, there is a substantial amount of green waste on the verges. Is there any way that the Shire can collect this and store it for use at the Farrall Road facility, or does the contractor keep the mulch?Director Built and Natural Environment advised that the Shire is looking at a different service by providing Shire officers to undertake this work. Regarding the green waste, it is currently collected and taken to Mathieson Road where another contractor then collects it and reused for mulch in commercial settings.

Against:None

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"E-rates winner
This year, to encourage property owners to sign-up for e-rates, we offered a special prize for those who subscribed by Friday 19 September.
This prize is a credit of up to $4,000 towards the winner’s 2025/26 rates!
E-rates come with great benefits including email delivery and reminders, electronic tip passes and reduced paper waste.
We had 3,029 ratepayers subscribe and if you haven’t done so already, I encourage all property owners to sign up for e-rates via the Shire’s website. 
I’ll ask the Deputy Shire President to conduct the draw.
Congratulations to FJ Thompson (Assessment No. 113843) !
 
Thank you – Deputy Shire President Luke Ellery
I would also like to thank Councillor Ellery for his service as Deputy President of the Shire of Mundaring. I acknowledge and thank Cr Ellery for the support and advice he has provided me over the past 5 months. It's most appreciated.
Council will consider nominations for the Deputy Shire President at a Special Council meeting to be held on Tuesday 28 October, following the Local Government elections.

Diwali – The festival of lights
The Shire of Mundaring acknowledges the celebration of the Indian festival of Diwali, which falls on Monday 20 October. This festival, also known as the Festival of Lights, symbolises the enduring values of hope, renewal and the victory of light over darkness. 
We wish all who are celebrating, a bright and prosperous Diwali.

Community Event Grants Recipients
I’m pleased to announce the recipients of this year’s Community Event Grants, which support not-for-profit community groups to deliver events that bring our community together, attract visitors and celebrate the very best of our Shire.
Each year, these grants help fund a diverse range of activities, from art exhibitions and festivals to family fun days and cultural celebrations.
This year’s recipients include:
  • Art in the Hills Open Studios – kicking off this Saturday 18 October is a week-long celebration of local art and creativity across our hills communities.
  • Whim Festival – in Mt Helena is back on 26 October. Its an inclusive, family-friendly festival featuring live music and a mural will be painted in real time during the event!
  • Darlington Arts Festival – is back on 1st and 2nd November and is one of the Hills’ most iconic community-run events, showcasing local art and artisans food and performances.
  • Day in the Forrest – in Glen marking its 10th anniversary on Saturday 6 December, a fantastic event that brings people together to enjoy music, markets and the beautiful natural surrounds of Glen Forrest
These events are organised by volunteers and the Shire of Mundaring is so proud to provide significant funding and support. 

Community-Wide Events Grant Recipients
I’m also pleased to advise that at the Grant Selection Committee meeting held on Tuesday, 7 October, all three applications for a Community-wide Events Grant were approved as follows:
  • Swan View Community Association – Swan View Christmas Celebration – $5000
  • Darlington Theatre Players (dba Marloo Theatre) – Jeeves at Sea Theatrical Production – $5000
  • Bibbul Ngarma Aboriginal Association Inc – Mandoon Bilya BioBlitz Festival – $4993
 
The Mandoon Gilya BioBlitz Festival is scheduled for this Saturday, 18 October, at Sculpture Park.
All applicants were thrilled to receive the funding and are looking forward to delivering some fantastic community events with the support of Shire of Mundaring.
 
Citizenship Awards – Nominations Now Open
Nominations are now open for the 2026 Shire of Mundaring Citizenship Awards.
These awards recognise and celebrate the people who make an outstanding contribution to our community, from volunteers and local leaders to young people and community groups who go above and beyond.
There are four categories this year: Young Citizen of the Year, Inspirational Volunteer, Access Mundaring, and Long Service. I encourage everyone to think about someone who deserves recognition and to submit a nomination before the closing date.
This is our opportunity to shine a light on the individuals and groups whose efforts help make the Shire of Mundaring a stronger, more connected community.

Local Government Elections - Reminder
It is now too late to post your ballot however you can you can hand-deliver your ballot to the Shire Admin Building during business hours, or between 8am and 6pm on polling day this Saturday 18 October. 
We extend our best to all candidates in the upcoming election.
Election time also gives me the opportunity to extend heartfelt thanks, on behalf of Council, to our Councillors and external committee members for their unwavering dedication and service.

Thank you – Audit and Risk Committee members
Firstly, on behalf of Shire of Mundaring Council, I’d like to sincerely thank our external members of the Audit and Risk Committee over the past two years – Shona Zulsdorf and Tony Wittcomb.
Their dedication, knowledge and professionalism have made a real difference to our work, helping to strengthen governance and improve risk management in our   Shire.
Council truly appreciates their involvement and the valuable insights shared during their time on the committee.

Thank you – Councillor Doug Jeans
Finally, on behalf of Council I extend our thanks to Councillor Doug Jeans for his long and dedicated service as he retires from Council on Saturday.
Elected from a field of eight candidates in 2015, Cr Jeans has proudly represented Central Ward for 10 years. During this time, he has contributed across many committees including the Audit and Risk Committee, Bush Fire Advisory Committee, Environmental Advisory Group, CEOPRC, Perth Airport Municipal Group and the Australia Day Citizenship Awards Committee.
Cr Jeans also served on the Eastern Metropolitan Regional Council (EMRC) for eight years, including as Deputy Chair from 2019 to 2021. One of his key portfolio interests has been waste management, where he played a pivotal role in establishing a Containers for Change depot at Mundaring Community Recycling Centre.
Cr Jeans was also instrumental in Council’s original opposition to Structure Plan 34 North Stoneville, moving the motion that recommended refusal of the proposal to the Western Australian Planning Commission. In recognition of his service, he received a Merit Award from the Western Australian Local Government Association (WALGA) in 2022.
We also extend our gratitude to Doug’s wife Carla, who has been a steadfast source of support during his decade of service.
I would now like to present Cr Jeans with a letter of appreciation and offer you the opportunity to say a few words.

Cr Jeans responded thanking the Shire President for her kind words and he also thanked his wife and the wider community for their support and feedback provided over the past 10 years. Cr Jeans believes he has achieved his goals from when he started out on Council and that was to listen to the community, to provide on-going scrutiny of the budget process and to be fair and reasonable in the decision making process. Summary of QuestionsSummary of Response
Megan Rhodes - Chidlow
1.Given that many new residents are purchasing large blocks in Chidlow and surrounding areas and clearing all mature trees simply because they do not like them, what steps is the Shire taking to protect tree canopy and the rural character of our community, and will Council consider introducing a tree retention policy similar to those adopted by other WA local governments?
Director Place and Community advised that it is noted that the Shire’s Local Planning Scheme No. 4 protects from the clearing of native vegetation on private land without a development application, meaning rigorous assessment takes place to ensure that any removal of vegetation is only supported when not of a high environmental/ecological value. The Shire’s various Departments conduct in-depth assessment of subdivisions and development applications which involve any intended clearing of native vegetation. Furthermore, the natural environment, including native vegetation on private property is protected under the Shire’s Local Planning Scheme No 4 and other environmental legislation (Environmental Protection Act and EPBC Act 1999). This is regardless of zoning. Shire approval is also required to remove any native vegetation, including trees, shrubs, herbs and grasses unless an exemption applies. As such an introduction of a Local Planning Policy for tree retention would be considered to have little-to-no bearing on the Shire’s ability to retain trees on private land as the Shire’s current planning framework outlined in Local Planning Scheme No. 4 already contains a set of provisions in Clause 5.7.12 that protects vegetation on private land. Specifically, the provisions apply to any ‘ringbarking, cutting down, topping, removal, or injuring or wilful destruction of any local native vegetation to be prohibited unless meeting the exemption criteria under 5.7.12.3”. Building Permits which are seeking exemptions from planning approval are being checked at officer level to ensure that this provision is upheld before any development on land occurs. As such, any future local planning policy to govern the retention of a tree on private land would be considered null and void for the reasons of duplication as this is already covered in the Local Planning Scheme. 
2.If someone has a private residence and is cutting down trees what can one do or could you email me in regards to that?
Director Place & Community advised that if someone is doing that they are required to have planning approval to do so. The simple thing would be to contact the Shire and ask if that property have planning approval to remove trees. If they don't the Shire can investigate the matter. If there are any queries for any particular problems on properties residents can advise the Shire.
Eric Smith - Glen Forrest
1.Recently, a mobile traffic signage trailer with government plates was placed in front of the Mundaring Shires Administration Centre. Quite bold in its presentation. Why was not one of the $50,000 LED signs that we have, not placed in a similar location as a permanent advertising meeting for events etc. Why has the progress of an LED sign in front of the administration centre not proceeded?
Director Built & Natural Environment advised that the Shire did do a business case to the councillors looking at that possibility. In doing that, the Shire reviewed the Main Roads guidelines for advertising of digital signs and that provided a number of restrictions that prohibited the type of signs that we had previously in the parks. It was really limited so the only thing that could potentially be done was something like a variable message board with large lettering with static lettering. But there is an ongoing concern with safety of that intersection as well, so the Shire are contemplating not putting variable message boards there going forward, and therefore not use that location at all other than perhaps for very static nonilluminated signs.
2.Mundaring Shire in recent years in budget deliberations has been spending a substantial amount on replacement of vehicles and major equipment, which in many cases need not have been replaced because of longer warranties and longer life of much of the modern day equipment and seem to have limited usage considering the lithium batteries installed and limited resale value. Why are we still following the age-old past of low mileage, service life and time as a guide to replacement of vehicles and equipment when manufacturers are offering longer warranty periods and inclusiveness of service as well?
The Chief Executive Officer advised that the Shire is currently in the process of recruiting a fleet manager and one of their first tasks will be to review the turnover rates. Currently the way the Shire turn over its light vehicle fleet, the parameters are around 100,000 kilometres or four or five years, which is pushing the changeover out to a reasonable time period and similarly with heavy fleets. It is something the Shire is very mindful of, but certainly looking to be a bit more strategic moving forward in developing a plan which will be presented to Council.
3.When the Shire's contractor sweeps the footpaths throughout the Shire, is there an inspection ever done on the quality and cleanliness of the work done or is it just relying on the contractor's honesty and integrity of a good job done and we ratepayers are paying substantial dollars for this service, as indicated in monthly payments to contractors?
Director Built & Natural Environment advised that there are inspections done, however, they are spot inspections as obviously the Shire is not able to follow the footpath sweeper but the quality of work is checked on that basis.
4.The Shire is paying quite a substantial amount of our ratepayer's income on traffic management and control in various tasks. Is there a study of or the assessment done by the Shire to employ staff as traffic controllers as against the cost of hiring contracted traffic controllers? The Shire staffer then could be employed in other areas when not on traffic controlling.
Director Built & Natural Environment advised that the Shire has looked at bringing that service in-house and are actively reviewing as costs have been escalating. The Shire will continue to pursue and look if that is an option.
5.Is it is planned for this year to purchase more EVs when there seems to be a better response to hybrid type vehicles, and why are we purchasing high priced utilities like Isuzu's when a lesser expensive similar type of utility could be purchased?
Director Built & Natural Environment advised that there is currently a review underway of the Shire's fleet in terms of conversion to electric vehicles. The Shire have trialled some fully electric vehicles in the fleet already and the Shire is also contemplating an electric utility. There is currently a BYD available for that and the Shire is looking at that as a trial also. When finalising the fleet review, light plant will also be included.

The CEO advised that he had received one nomination for Deputy Shire President for the ensuing two years, for Cr Luke Ellery nominated by Cr Mehta.

The CEO called for any further nominations, then declared the nomination period closed.   

As no further nominations were received, the CEO declared Cr Luke Ellery to the position of Deputy Shire President at the Shire of Mundaring for the ensuing two years.

Declaration by the Deputy President
Section 2.29 requires that a person elected by the council as deputy president has to make a declaration in the prescribed form before acting in the office.

Regulation 13 of the Local Government (Constitution) Regulations 1995 provides the prescribed form, Form 7, and the following (in part): 

(3) A declaration required by section 2.29 to be made by a person elected as a councillor, deputy mayor or deputy president is to be made before an authorised person. …

(5) In this regulation —
authorised person means a person before whom a statutory declaration can be made under the Oaths, Affidavits and Statutory Declarations Act 2005.

Note: the Chief Executive Officer is an authorised person under the Oaths, Affidavits and Statutory Declarations Act 2005.

Cr Ellery made a declaration of office of Deputy Shire President (using the prescribed form),under the Oaths, Affidavits and Statutory Declarations Act 2005, before the CEO.

ALTERNATIVE MOTION 
Moved by:Cr Daw
Seconded by:Cr Grills
That Council:
 
Recommends that the West Australian Planning Commission (WAPC) REFUSE Structure Plan No.82 (SP82) - 
Lot 100 (4005) Lilidale Rd Chidlow, Lots 2507 and 2508 (2000) Sertorio Rd Chidlow and Lot 2417 (475) Kerun Rd Chidlow, for the following reasons:
 
A)
1. SP82 does not represent orderly and proper planning for the locality. The SP82 proposed development is incompatible with its setting, including —
(i) the incompatibility of the development with the desired future character of its setting; and
(ii) the relationship of the development to development on adjoining land in the locality.
Thus negatively affecting the amenity of the locality
 
2. Incompatible with LPS4
SP82 proposes rural residential development with lot sizes of 1ha in a Rural Residential 2 (RR2) zoned land and therefore does not comply with s. 5.9.1.1 of Shire of Mundaring LPS4 and the Scheme Maps which designate the SP82 area as RR2
 
3. Rural Character
SP 82 contravenes the principle as stated in the Local Planning Strategy that the Shire continues to support a series of discreet villages separated by rural buffers as in this instance of SP82, in the rural 'buffer' area, SP82 proposes smaller, 1 ha blocks, that are out of character with the established rural amenity of the area.
 
4. Bushfire Risk
According to DFES, SP82 represents an unacceptable bushfire risk. The Bushfire Management Plan (BMP) does not appear to adequately address the policy requirements of State Planning Policy 3.7 (SPP3.7), because it is in an extreme bushfire area with linkages to Karakamaia Sanctuary, Wooroloo Regional Park and Lake Leschenaultia Conservation Park and other bushfire prone bush reserves on Council, Unallocated Crown Land and private land in the immediate vicinity of the proposed SP82. Therefore Council considers that the Precautionary Principle applies as the BMP does not sufficiently mitigate bushfire risks.
 
5. SP82 is not connected to reticulated water as per the requirement of SPP 2.5 Rural Planning. See Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development (DPIRD) submission No38
 
6. Environmental Impacts
SP82 contains 1592 potential Black Cockatoo breeding trees on site and this should trigger referral under the Commonwealth EPBC Act as clearing for infrastructure and housing required to comply with SPP3.7, will see the 'modification' (removal) of significant native trees and other remnant vegetation.
Structure Plan 82 goes against many of the principles entailed in the Shire's Local Biodiversity Strategy and Council Plan of protecting natural areas and biodiversity.
 
7. The LWMS does not demonstrate that water quality issues associated with the development and subdivision of SP82 have been considered and could negatively impact Cookes Brook/Wooroloo Brook i.e., significantly increased number of effluent disposal systems have the potential to impact the Cookes Brook and wetlands at the lower southern end of the SP site
 
8. SP82 has steep sloping contours in some parts causing potentially serious (wind) and water erosion and serious flooding of downhill lots and is a serious bushfire hazard. Noting slopes over 10 degrees are classified as extreme. See Department of Fire and Emergency Services (DFES) submission No57
 
9. Traffic impacts 
Many local residents in their submissions using their local knowledge and experience add that Lilidale Rd and Rosedale Roads would prove unsuitable for bushfire fire escape routes based on local population trying to escape a bushfire along with tourists visiting Lake Leschenaultia in summer.
 
B) Council acknowledges that all submissions made on Structure Plan 82 have been considered.
LOST 2/7
For:Cr Daw, Cr Grills
Against:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Ellery, Cr Cicchini, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Strutt, Cr Woods

Summary of Questions
Summary of Response
Mimi Scully
1The Australian Wildlife Conservancy is a global conservation leader. Karakamia Sanctuary is the birthplace of the organisation and plays a pivotal role in the ongoing protection of critically endangered native species (for eg Woylie). Additionally, Karakamia plays an important role in providing source populations for the re-establishment of threatened and endangered species in WA and across the nation. The AWC is concerned with the development which abuts sections of our southern boundary.  AWC requests that building envelopes 1 - 9 (from plan dated 6th August 2025), and 47-53 (from plan dated 9th Oct 2024), and the associated access roads be removed from the Subdivision Concept (dated 6th Aug 2025). This will provide a buffer between the nationally recognised sanctuary and the proposed development. 
Manager Community Planning advised the Shire’s recommendation was that building envelopes being shown only for lots with environmental constraints. Furthermore, the revised plan has a total of 48 lots, reduced from the envisaged number of lots that formed part of the initial application, hence why there is now no lots 49-53. Access road north of proposed lot 7 and 8 has been recommended to be removed as it proposes a dead end with no benefit to bushfire access and egress. 
2Cats, both domestic and feral, are the major driver of extinctions in Australia. A domestic cat kills approximately 186 animals per year (University of Sydney). Within the proposed area, if each building envelope has one cat, this equates to 8556 animals being killed each year.  Considering the proximity of the proposed development to a nationally recognized wildlife sanctuary, can the council enforce greater restrictions on domestic pets permitted within the proposed area?
Manager Community Planning noted there aren’t any planning mechanisms in terms of framework or provisions that specify development standards to mitigate impacts of feral animals to this sanctuary. However, there are rules and restrictions around keeping cats are captured with the Shire’s “Keeping of Cats Local Laws”.

Shire President added the Shire's "Keeping of Cats Local Law" and the State Government has recently advised that they are amending the legislation to provide Local Governments to amend their Local Law to include containment provisions. As a Council, we have decided we will review the Local Law. Currently waiting on the State Government to provide the updated legislation so the Shire's review is meaningful. 
Eric Smith
1Are the old Shire built bus shelters across the Shire, going to be removed now that there are TransPerth bus stops?Director Built & Natural Environment confirmed the Shire installed some lean-tos some time ago. Overtime, these have become redundant and have been slowly removed as they do not meet current codes.
2When the Shire replaces vehicles and equipment, how are the old vehicles and equipment disposed, and where is it advertised?This question was taken on notice.
Peter Brazier
1Has the developer referred Structure Plan SP82 to the Federal Department of Environment (DCCEEW) as the proposal affects three listed endangered Black Cockatoo species as required under the EPBC Act?
Manager Community Planning did not believe the applicant has referred this to DCCEEW for federal approval as of yet.
2In relation to the Shire's Local Planning Scheme update, what is the status and projected completion date for the new Local Planning Scheme?Manager Community Planning confirmed the Shire is currently drafting the schemes, with public consultation to occur next year and having it gazetted in 2028.
Christian Jackson-Stegner
1Is the Shire of Mundaring able to dictate lot and property sizes depending on the surroundings in the neighbourhood town/semi-rural/rural towards the developer.Manager Community Planning advised in terms of property sizes, these are determined by the R-Coding in residential zones, and Local Planning Scheme provisions in non-residential zoned land. A minimum lot size is generally outlined within the Local Planning Scheme, which is an LG planning instrument.
2Does WA State and Federal law break local law regarding property sizes in development areas?Manager Community Planning noted the planning hierarchy is within the Western Australian Planning system, the state framework holds greater weight to that of a local planning instrument. Ie, the Planning and Development Regulations 2015 overrides any conflict with a Local Planning Scheme.
Chris Bond
1Regarding the Brooking Road extension, is it common practice for the Shire to have little to no community consultation prior to then announcing planned/proposed starting dates?Director Built & Natural Environment advised this particular project has been planned for some time and has been discussed with community as it progressed. In May of this year, communications was sent to over 150 residents within the vicinity as well as information provided on the Shire's website.
2The brief mentions linking to existing infrastructure, why is the proposed Brooking Road extension significantly wider than the surrounding roads? and why is the footpath significantly wider and leads to nowhere?Director Built & Natural Environment advised Brooking Road and Beacon Road have been upgraded to a wider standard. A particular section of the proposed extension of Brooking Road is wider when it meets the heritage trail to create a crossing, besides this section, it remains consistent.

The proposed footpaths will connect to the Richardson Road footpath at the southern end and will extend to Parker Road.
Adrian Julitz
1Regarding SP82, has there been an environmental assessment on how it will impact Karakamia Sanctuary?Coordinator Environment and Sustainability advised this will be done as part of the subdivision process.
2How can Council make a judgement on this subdivision when there has been no environmental assessment?Manager Community Planning advised the structure plan is being assessed tonight, the final details and specifics around the subdivision itself will be dealt with at a later stage with the Western Australian Planning Commission.
Frankie Barbour
1With respect to the proposed water subsidy motion put forward by Doug Jeans in October that was deferred to December, which Councillors are willing to meet with us before the December meeting to discuss any modifications, and who will speak to the motion now that Doug Jeans is no longer a Councillor?Chief Executive Officer advised that the community can email Councillors and speak with them individually. Their numbers and email addresses are available on the Shire's website.

Regarding the notice of motion, Council will pick up the debate where it was left off at the previous Council meeting.

2During the transition period until the Shire installs its Gold Standard Sustainable Water Supply Project, that it's only fair that the Glen Forrest community gardens usual agreement remain in place?

3Regarding the new bike pump track, it is very elevated and will displace a lot of the wet land flooding from its usual places. Will the works be completed before June next year when the rain sets, particularly the drainage system.

Moved by:Cr Mehta

That Council:

Requests the Chief Executive Officer to cease all activities associated with the Brooking Road Extension and Falls Road Bridge Replacement pending a full briefing to Council detailing:

  1. The proposed road elevation and its potential amenity impacts on adjacent residential properties;
  2. The proposed road elevation and drainage, flooding, and runoff impacts on adjacent residential properties;
  3. The hydrological, sedimentary, and ecological impacts of the proposed works on Jane Brook and its catchment;
  4. The extent of tree clearing, canopy loss, and impacts on native vegetation and wildlife habitat;
  5. Outcomes of community engagement.

CARRIED 8/1

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":" Alcoa Withdrawal 
 
The Presiding Member wished to share some welcome news for our community. 
 
You may have seen in the news that Alcoa has confirmed it will withdraw its plans for exploration across the Perth Hills. This decision reflects the strong community voice we have seen over many months, and the ongoing advocacy from Shire of Mundaring. 
 
Protecting the natural environment is a core value for our community. The withdrawal of these exploration plans gives residents confidence that the landscapes we care about can continue to be enjoyed and preserved. 
 
I thank everyone who raised their concerns, and I acknowledge the State Government representative and local community groups for their work in keeping this issue front of mind. This outcome shows how powerful a collective community effort can be. 
 
Bilgoman Aquatic Centre Sustainable Heating Upgrade  
 
Bilgoman Aquatic Centre will soon receive a major sustainable heating upgrade. 
 
The installation of a new pool heating system will significantly reduce energy use and operating costs while keeping the pool warm and comfortable for swimmers.  
 
This project supports our long-term sustainability goals and helps maintain Bilgoman as a valued community facility. 
 
The upgrade is funded through the Community Energy Upgrades Fund, with Shire of Mundaring contributing half. 
 
I thank the Federal Government for its support and look forward to delivering a more energy-efficient and environmentally responsible facility for our community. 
 
Parkerville Cricket Nets
 
The new cricket training nets at Parkerville Oval are now complete and open for community use. 
 
This upgrade provides stronger playing surfaces, improved safety, and a modern facility that can support junior and senior players throughout the season. The new design meets the needs of our growing cricket community and supports active, healthy lifestyles in the Perth Hills. 
 
I would like to thank the local clubs for their input during the planning and construction stages. I also acknowledge the State Government for its support. 
 
These new nets will give players of all ages a better place to train and get ready for a big summer of cricket. 
 
Environmental Art Project Banners  
 
Finally, I am pleased to announce the launch of our new Environmental Art Project banners, now on display in Mundaring Town Centre. 
 
These banners showcase the creativity of local young people and celebrate their connection to the environment. Each artwork reflects how our next generation sees the Perth Hills, from its forests and wildlife to its sense of place. 
 
This project supports youth creativity and gives young artists a public platform to share their ideas. It also brightens our town centres and reminds us all why caring for our natural environment matters. 
 
I thank the participating students, their schools, and our judging panel for their hard work. Summary of Questions
Summary of Response
Eric Smith - Glen Forrest
1Does the Mundaring Council encourage local small business, if the answer is yes, then where does that fit into the Mundaring Shire's promotion of the tourism umbrella of encouraging visitors to the Mundaring Shire and the promotion of small local, home type businesses?Director Place and Community advised that the Shire does support local businesses through a range of different initiatives, including through components of the Shire's Planning Scheme and Strategy.  The Shire is also developing a range of different initiatives to "buy local" through tourism and attracting visitors to the region to spend at local businesses.  The Shire has a whole raft of initiatives that are considered and all outlined in the Shire's Tourism & Economic Strategy.
The Shire President also advised that the Shire works closely with the Mundaring Chamber of Commerce and the Shire President and CEO meet quarterly with the Chamber of Commerce to discuss how the Shire can support the Chamber better.
Pam Riordan - President - Eastern Hills Wildflower Society
1In 2019 to 2020 money was allocated on the budget for repairs to a disintegrating wall at the Octagonal Hall, Glen Forrest which is a heritage listed building.  I would like to know what's happened to the money?Director Built and Natural Environment advised that the money has been carried forward into the current budget to enable the Shire to complete the works.
2When will the front wall of Octagonal Hall be replaced or repaired given that it's a safety issue and the plastic bollards have been in place for 4 years?Director Built and Natural Environment advised that because the building is heritage listed, the Shire engaged a consultant to assess whether the wall had significance. The conclusion from that was that whilst the building had strong significance, the wall which was built slightly later, had some significance.  Director Built and Natural Environment has written to the Heritage Council to ascertain what limitations that might mean for the wall, given there is some significance attached to it.  The Shire has previously approached stonemasons to try and replicate what is there without any success and are hoping to demolish the wall and replace with something else, however, require guidance from the Heritage Council with strong intent to have finished in the first half of next year.
Greg Jones - Stoneville Parkerville Progress Association
1Following the recent Stoneville Parkerville Progress Association petition of 174 signatures submitted to the Shire on 24 November, when and where will the Shire be conducting an open forum community consultation to present the final design details for the Brooking Road extension to the community and not just to a few individual one-to-one selective engagement meetings as currently attempted by the Shire as so called community engagement?The Chief Executive Officer advised that the current plan the Shire officer officers have implemented is the Shire has engaged directly with the adjoining land owners to Brooking Road to gage their response to the works the Shire is planning to undertake.  The Shire has also identified a larger area of residents in the proximity of Brooking Road and the Shire has both emailed and written letters to all those residents explaining the project, providing additional detail with regards to the design. In that letter the Shire has also provided a specific contact if residents wanted to reach out and ask more questions.  In respect to a public meeting, the Shire is not planning on having a public meeting at this point.  The Chief Executive Officer is more than happy to catch up with Mr Jones to talk through any concerns he may have on the project.
2Does the Council know that the Shire is breach of its Permit to Clear issued by DWER in 2021 that requires conditional minimum of 55 endangered cockatoo habitat offset trees to be planted and maintained, whereas now only 24 habitat offset trees actually exist and that many of them are in poor condition and may not survive this summer?

Director Built and Natural Environment advised that part of the condition was to monitor and report on those so if any were not to survive the Shire will need to replace those, so there is a commitment there for that to happen.  They will be monitored and if required replaced.
John Wilson - Mundaring
1It is noticeable that there are more electric bikes coming on the walk trails now and also electric scooters.  Has the Council have any ideas on how to handle this change?The Chief Executive Officer advised that this is the first he has heard of that specific concern.  Electric scooters and bikes are a challenge across the state at the moment.  The Shire will have a discussion internally with respect to how big an issue it is and if there is anything the Shire can put in place.  It is very challenging in reserves and on tracks to manage that sort of activity but the Shire will look into it.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Before commencing tonight's Special Council meeting, the Presiding Member would like to acknowledge the tragic events in Bondi over the weekend.
 
On behalf of Council, we extend our deepest sympathies to the families, friends, and all those affected.
 
Our thoughts are with the wider community at this difficult time.
 
I would also like to take a moment to remind our community that we are now well into bushfire season.
 
Conditions can change quickly, so it is important to stay informed and prepared.
 
I encourage everyone to sign up to the Shire’s SMS alerts and download the Emergency WA app.
If you see a fire, report it immediately to Triple Zero (000). Please do not contact local bushfire brigades directly.
 
As this is our final Special Council Meeting for the year, I want to sincerely thank my fellow Councillors and Shire staff.
 
Your dedication, professionalism, and commitment to our community throughout the year is greatly appreciated.
 
I also want to wish everyone a safe and restful Christmas and holiday period.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Glen Forrest Pump (Jump) Track
The Presiding Member was pleased to share that the Glen Forrest Pump (Jump) Track is nearing completion and will be ready to ride very soon.

This has been a strongly community-led project, shaped by local riders, residents and the Glen Forrest Residents and Ratepayers Association, and it’s been great to see that collaboration come together on site.

To celebrate the delivery of the track, we’ll be holding an official opening at Morgan John Morgan Park in Glen Forrest on Saturday 21 February from 5pm to 7pm.
It will be a relaxed, family-friendly event with a ribbon-cutting, food and music, and the chance to see local riders enjoying the track and bringing the space to life.
I’d encourage the community to come along, soak up the atmosphere and be part of celebrating a project that reflects strong local input and energy.

Acknowledgement of Bravery - Austin Appelbee
The Presiding Member acknowledged the recent heroic efforts from a neighbour who has been much in the press, Austin Appelbee, who does attend a school in the Shire of Mundaring in his efforts to swim a courageous distance in service to save his family, demonstrating his courage and his perseverance.

Acknowledgement - Emergency Service Providers
The Presiding Member also acknowledge the Shire's emergency service providers and in another stellar effort in a recent fire that was in the Boya / Helena Valley / Darlington, corner of Glen Road and Victor Road. Summary of Questions
Summary of Response
 Janette Huston - Gidgegannup
1
Why is the Shire actively moving to shut down local growers such as the Raw Larder and a few others, and why is Twin Leaf Farm now being pursued by what seems to be overly aggressive junior planning officers?
Director Place and Community advised that while she is unable to speak about the details of individual businesses or cases, she can share how the Shire approaches these situations in general. The Shire’s intention is not to close down local growers or small operators. The Shire values the contribution these businesses make to our community. The Shire's role is to work alongside landowners and local operators to help ensure their activities meet the requirements of the relevant legislation and planning approvals. The Shire's aim is always to support people to achieve compliance wherever possible, not to penalise them.
2
Why is the Shire not responding to emails and requests for information from these people? 
Director Place and Community advised the Shire is actively communicating with landowners whenever a compliance matter arises, and does respond to emails and enquiries. If anyone feels they haven’t received a response or they’re still waiting on information, they are encouraged to contact the Director Place and Community directly who is more than happy to follow up and make sure their query is addressed. 
 Eric Smith - Glen Forrest
1
Referring to the up and coming budget, will councillors scrutinise the budget submissions, particularly in the purchase and replacement of equipment, and in particular the vehicle fleet and its use?
The Chief Executive Officer advised that Council and individual Councillors get access to, in the context of fleet, the Shire's entire replacement program or what is being proposed to be replaced and then Council is able to scrutinise that.
2
This financial year budgeted for around $4 million for the replacement of vehicles and equipment. That was the total, what was the total cost of the purchase of the vehicles and equipment and the various vehicles and equipment?
The Chief Executive Officer advised that he would be unable to answer the question in its entirety, given that the Shire is still working through its replacement program, so not all the plant has been replaced. In the Council agenda there is a list of capital items that are due for replacement and all the individual items are planned and specified in that replacement schedule. The Shire is also happy to provide Mr Smith with a summary of what has been replaced prior to this point.
 Daniel I'Ons - Mundaring
1
I live on Craig Street and my small unit is vehicle accessible via Hodgson Lane. There's a proposal for some units between Hodgson Lane, Fenton Street and the Highway. From what I can make out, there's vehicle access only to this new unit block from either Fenton Street or Hodgson Lane. What is the proposed vehicle access to this unit block that's going to be coming in and is Hodgson Lane, the way that it's built, capable of taking the traffic from the proposed unit block?
The Chief Executive Officer advised that unfortunately he does not have the exact details to provide a response, however, a detailed written response will be provided to Mr I'Ons and the written response will be publishn the agenda for the next Council meeting.
 Janette Huston - Gidgegannup
3
Can the Council require that any proposed closure, or any effort by the shire to stop a business, stallholder, or trader from operating, be formally raised as an issue for Council review, so the Council stays informed and can intervene to support those affected?
Director Place and Community advised that the Shire’s Administration has the statutory obligation to look into compliance matters and ensure the requirements of relevant legislation are followed. When appropriate, Council is kept informed and briefed on these issues. The Shire's aim is always to approach this work in a fair, transparent, and supportive way for everyone involved.
4
Does the Council have a policy that actively supports and enables local businesses to thrive, protecting them from excessive red‑tape and bureaucratic hurdles? If no such policy exists, could one be created?
Director Place and Community advised that, yes, Council has been very clear in its support for helping local businesses grow and succeed. This commitment is reflected in the Council Plan, which guides how the Shire meets its community’s needs and priorities, including supporting local businesses and industry to thrive.
5
Does the Council aim to nurture local businesses and independent stallholders so that our hills community can retain its diverse, vibrant character? Or is the focus simply on backing large chains such as Coles, Woolworths, and Aldi?
Director Place and Community advised that the Shire is absolutely committed to supporting local businesses and helping them succeed. At the same time, the Shire also has a responsibility to listen to the broader community and ensure that activities operate safely and in line with public health requirements. The Shire's aim is always to balance support for local enterprise with the wellbeing and expectations of the community as a whole.
 Eric Smith - Glen Forrest
3
There's been many road upgrades within the Shire using the hot mix resurfacing and road reconstruction.  What is or will be the total cost of this project, and this includes all roads within the Shire boundary?
Director Built and Natural Environment advised that he did not have all those details to hand, however, will provide a written response to Mr Smith.
4
Any progress on the employment of an officer who, as I understand, task will be to sort the fleet assets and where we are at to this date?
Director Built and Natural Environment advised that, as mentioned at the last Council meeting, the Shire does have a new Fleet Coordinator who has commenced approximately 3 weeks ago.

RESOLUTION NUMBER:C-3-3-2026 
MOTION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Woods
Seconded by:Cr Ellery
That Council:
 
  1. Support the request made by the Swan View Football Club and provide a financial contribution towards the cost of installing an electronic scoreboard at Brown Park;
  1. By absolute majority, contributes $20,000 to the project, pending the outcome of the Swan View Football Club's application to the Telstra Footy Grants Round 1 Program for the electronic scoreboard;
  1. Advises the Swan View Football Club that the Shire of Mundaring would project manage the purchase and installation of the scoreboard, which would become an asset of the Shire of Mundaring for the purposes of insurance and maintenance, including electronic components and upgrading as required of the structure; and
  1. Upgrade priorities to be delivered for the Brown Park Master Plan and the Recreation Facilities Informing Plan to be considered as part of the 2026 review of the Long Term Financial Plan.

CARRIED BY ABSOLUTE MAJORITY 9/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Cicchini, Cr Grills, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Strutt, Cr Woods
Against:None

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Citizenship Ceremony
Last week the Shire proudly welcomed 61 new Australian citizens during our Citizenship Ceremony at Mundaring Arena.
These ceremonies are always a special moment for our community. Each person has chosen to make Australia and our hills community their home.
Our newest citizens come from countries across the world including New Zealand, the United Kingdom, Mexico, Vietnam, Brazil, Sweden, Pakistan, the Philippines, Afghanistan, Canada and many more.
On behalf of Council, I congratulate each of them and welcome them warmly to our community.
 
Brown Park Master Plan Consultation
The Shire is currently seeking community feedback on the Brown Park Master Plan.
Brown Park is one of our most important recreation spaces and is used by many sporting clubs, families and community groups.
The Master Plan will guide how the precinct evolves over the coming years so it continues to support sport, recreation and community connection while protecting the natural environment.
I encourage everyone with an interest in Brown Park to take a look at the concept plans and share their feedback.
