Summary of Questions
Summary of Response
Debra Bishop - Save Perth Hills
1Has the Shire of Mundaring CEO instructed the Shire's lawyer Craig Slarke from McLeods to lodge a formal response by this Friday the 13th of March to Satterley Property Group's application for the State Tribunal to reopen Satterley's North Stoneville appeal case and introduce new material? if not, why not?
The Chief Executive Officer advised that he is currently talking with the Shire's solicitor, who is in liaison with the State Solicitor's Office about their submission.  The Shire will make a determination whether there is a need for the Shire to make a submission or whether the Shire's solicitor believes that the Shire just support the State Solicitor's Office submission.  As soon as he is advised of the Shire solicitor position, he will be advising Council.
2Why hasn't the Shire's website been undated to inform the community that Satterley is seeking to reopen its appeal case in the State Tribunal for proposed North Stoneville, which would further extend the decision that the community is waiting for, and given the Shire has known about the reopening submission by Satterley since February 13?
The Chief Executive Officer advised this question would be taken on notice.
John Bell - Mount Helena
1Will Council be treating the development of Town Planning Scheme Number 5 as a project whereby the various steps to completion will be managed by a Gantt chart. The dates for completion of key steps and the overall project plan to achieve delivery of TPS5 nor later than June 2028?
Manager Community Planning advised that from the Shire's point of view, a Gantt chart would be prepared as well as some contingency plans in the event that the key timeframes do push out slightly.

 

Louise Stelfox - Darlington Resident & Ratepayer Association
1Regarding responses to the Annual Electors' Motions, is the Shire willing to go above and beyond its minimum legislated requirements to support positive community and environmental actions?
The Chief Executive Officer advised that while this is the case, the responses are focused on trying to understand and get the best possible outcomes for the community.  Further it is the responsibility of the officer to provide recommendations to Council which balance a wide range of information and context.  The Chief Executive Officer reiterated that as an organisation there is a strong desire to be connected to the community.
2What is the Shire doing with the trees allocated under the Urban Canopy Grant Program and over the next four years, how will the Shire publicise the Treebait Program, which was announced in January 2025 to increase tree canopy in urban areas?
The Chief Executive Officer thanked Ms Stelfox for providing the question in advance, however, unfortunately he was not able to get the information so will take the question on notice and provide a detailed response as soon as possible.
Eric Smith - Glen Forrest
1In reference to tonight's agenda - Decision 16, AEM 17-2-2026 in reference to LED signs, we keep getting fobbed off with an LED sign at the front of this administration building to tell the community what's going on. Could Council please supply in writing the MRWA reasoning for the decision of not applying a position of an LED sign in front of or in proximity of the Mundaring Shire's Administration Centre?The Chief Executive Officer advised that in regards to the query about Council not listening or fobbing the community off, that's certainly not the case. Council gave consideration to this item approximately 12 months ago and based on the advice from officers determined that it wasn't practical to have an LED sign in front of the administration building.  In terms of the the written information from Main Roads, that is taken on notice and happy to provide more detail to Mr Smith once have determined what the Shire has.
Rob Greenwood - Stoneville
1 My question is in relation to Decision 10. That was in relation to the management plan for weed wattle removal. The particular item that was missing in the Council Officer's reply was the lack of liaison with Western Power. That was the key of the whole question, was to ask if Council could take steps to liaise with Western Power so that instead of cropping weed wattles underneath power lines, they could remove them completely?
The Shire President advised that the way agendas work is that Shire officers prepare recommendations to Council.  Council can change those recommendations.  An alternative motion is expected for that item in tonight's agenda.
2Regarding Decision 6 , the officer report focuses with what is planned in Swan View.It doesn't really answer the question of the 300 metres of fencing, which is lacking around the two football ovals in Hartung Street to prevent dogs from running onto Great Eastern Highway, which is a fairly minimal cost too. The officer's report really focuses on what's planned with Brown Park in Swan View, but doesn't focus on what we asked in the motion, which was that Council consider as a matter of priority completing the low perimeter fencing of the two dual-use football/dog exercise ovals in Hartung Street to make them safe for dog exercise due to their close proximity to Great Eastern Highland?The Shire President advised that matter is addressed in Annual Electors' Motion Decision 12.

Decision 1 - Communication Plan for Planning Reviews

RESOLUTION NUMBER:C-4-3-2026 
MOTION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Mehta
Seconded by:Cr Ellery
That Council notes decision AEM2.02.26 - Communication Plan for Planning Reviews and:
 
  1. Confirms that a comprehensive Community and Stakeholder Engagement Plan will be developed and implemented to support the review of the Local Planning Strategy and the preparation of Local Planning Scheme No. 5 and;
  1. Requests that the Community and Stakeholder Engagement Plan be circulated to the Shire's Residents and Ratepayers Associations for feedback prior to seeking Council endorsement for its implementation. 
CARRIED 9/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Cicchini, Cr Grills, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Strutt, Cr Woods
Against:None

Decision 4 - Mural Shire of Mundaring Entry Statement

RESOLUTION NUMBER:C-5-3-2026 
MOTION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Mehta
Seconded by:Cr Ellery
That Council notes AEM5-2-2026 - Mural Shire of Mundaring Entry Statement and requests the Shire President to write to Main Roads WA, Member for Kalamunda, Adam Hort MLA, Hon Klasey Hirst MLC and Hon Rita Saffioti MLA requesting a mural as part of the new Mundaring Entry Statement.  
CARRIED 9/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Cicchini, Cr Grills, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Strutt, Cr Woods
Against:None

Decision 5 - Feral Pests

RESOLUTION NUMBER:C-6-3-2026 
MOTION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Mehta
Seconded by:Cr Cicchini
That Council notes AEM6-2-2026 – Feral Pests, and updates its website to provide:
  1. Distinctions between the management of feral pests on public and private land; 
  2. Clear guidance on how to deal with feral pests; 
  3. Links to relevant information from government agencies; and
  4. Continue to implement the Shire's adopted Biodiversity Strategy regarding feral pest management. 

CARRIED 9/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Cicchini, Cr Grills, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Strutt, Cr Woods
Against:None

Decision 2 - Perth Hills Planning Strategy

RESOLUTION NUMBER:C-7-3-2026 
MOTION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Ellery
Seconded by:Cr Mehta
That Council notes decision AEM3.02.26 - Perth Hills Planning Policy and;

  1.  Confirms that the proposed policy aims and objectives are already supported by existing frameworks and legislation, and will be further strengthened through forthcoming planning frameworks, including the Shire’s Place Plan, the review of the Local Planning Strategy, and the revision of Local     Planning  Scheme No. 5; and
  2.  Confirms the decision aligns with the Advocacy Priorities (#10) for "changes to existing planning, policy and regulation to enable more favourable outcomes regarding balancing positive environmental outcomes with proposed development", and that a suitable State planning policy be considered in the Advocacy Plan.
CARRIED 9/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Cicchini, Cr Grills, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Strutt, Cr Woods
Against:None

Decision 3 - Christmas Festive Lighting in Shire Townsites

RESOLUTION NUMBER:C-8-3-2026 
MOTION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Ellery
Seconded by:Cr Grills
That Council notes decision AEM4.02.26 – Christmas Festive Lighting in Shire Townsites and considers scope and costs during budget deliberations.
CARRIED 9/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Cicchini, Cr Grills, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Strutt, Cr Woods
Against:None

 

Decision 8 - Legislation or Regulation in place to protect regulated native trees

MOTION
Moved by: Cr Ellery
Seconded by: Cr Mehta

That Council notes decision AEM 9.02.26 - Legislation or Regulation in place to protect regulated native trees and requests these decisions be considered in the Roadside Conservation Policy currently being reviewed by the Governance Committee.

8:12PM - Meeting Adjourned

RESOLUTION NUMBER:C-9-3-2026 
MOTION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Daw
Seconded by:Cr Cicchini
That the meeting be adjourned for a period of 5 minutes.
CARRIED 7/2
For:Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Cicchini, Cr Grills, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Strutt, Cr Woods
Against:Pres McNeil, Cr Ellery

CARRIED 9/0

RESOLUTION NUMBER:C-11-3-2026 
MOTION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Ellery

That Council notes decision AEM 9.02.26 - Legislation or Regulation in place to protect regulated native trees and requests these decisions be considered in the Roadside Conservation Policy, of which the scope, including applicability to private land, is currently being reviewed by the Governance Committee.

Decision 10 - Management Plan for permanent removal of highly flammable weed wattles

RESOLUTION NUMBER:C-12-3-2026 
MOTION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Ellery
Seconded by:Cr Heptinstall
That Council notes AEM11-2-2026 - Management Plan for permanent removal of highly flammable weed wattles and requests the Chief Executive Officer write to Western Power to ensure an appropriate risk management plan.
CARRIED 9/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Cicchini, Cr Grills, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Strutt, Cr Woods
Against:None

 

RESOLUTION NUMBER:C-13-3-2026 
MOTION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Ellery
Seconded by:Cr Woods
That Council:

  1. Acknowledges the contributions made by electors who participated in the 2026 Annual Electors' meeting;

  2. Thanked the residents and ratepayers who participated in the 2026 Annual Electors' Meeting; and

  3. In response to the decisions made at the 2026 Annual Electors' Meeting resolves: 

    Decisions 6, 7, 9 and Decisions 11 to 16 be carried by en-bloc Council Decision

Decision 6 - Re-open large dog area at dog park Swan View
 
That Council notes AEM7-2-2026 - Re-open large dog area at dog park Swan View and the intention to undertake remediation works to enable the temporary dog park to be fully reopened and take no additional action.

Decision 7 - Council to provide heat and light at Mt Helena Aquatic Centre 

That Council notes decision AEM8.02.26 - Provide heat and light at Mt Helena Aquatic Centre, and acknowledges that the recommendations and findings of the Aquatics Feasibility and Business Case Study, due for completion in June 2026, will guide future Council decisions regarding any potential upgrades, including heating and lighting, at the Mt Helena Aquatic Centre and take no additional action.

Decision 9 - Addition of a Pump Track at Mt Helena Skate Park

That Council notes decision AEM10 .02.26 - Pump Track at Mt Helena Skate Park, acknowledging that the Mt Helena BMX track is programmed for renewal in 29/30 allowing for a pump track to be explored as part of the planning process for that facility and take no additional action.

Decision 11 - Management Plan for William Adams Park/Jarrah Creek Dam 

That Council notes AEM12-2-2026 - Management Plan for William Adams Park/Jarrah Creek Dam and the proposed meeting with the group to discuss their list of suggested actions for William Adams Park/Jarrah Creek Dam.

Decision 12 - Fenced dog exercise areas within Mundaring/Stoneville town areas 

That Council notes AEM13-2-2026 - Fenced dog exercise areas within Mundaring/Stoneville town areas and considers this request in the context of all matters to be contemplated in place plans to be developed and future Council Plans.

Decision 13 - Signage on the Heritage Trails 

That Council notes AEM14-2-2026 - Signage on the Heritage Trails and the recently installed signage on the trail and take no additional action.

Decision 14 - Horse riders to use horse poo bags in Heritage trails, parks or near National Parks 

That Council notes AEM15-2-2026 - Horse riders to use horse poo bags in Heritage trails, parks or near National Parks and, as there is no ability to enforce the use of horse poo bags and take no additional action.

Decision 15 - Initiate a formal traffic pedestrian safety audit of the entry and exit points 

That Council notes AEM16-2-2026 - Initiate a formal traffic pedestrian safety audit of the entry and exit points, further noting that there are plans in place to review the entry and exit from the Administration building as part of a future stage of the town centre master plan and take no additional action.

Decision 16 - LED signs at the front or in proximity of the Administration Building 

That Council notes AEM17-2-2026 - LED signs at the front or in proximity of the Administration Building and, as the locations of the LED has already been chosen and the Admin Centre verge determined as unsuitable and take no additional action.
CARRIED 9/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Cicchini, Cr Grills, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Strutt, Cr Woods
Against:None

MOTION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Pres McNeil
Seconded by:Cr Mehta
That Council endorses the submission (Attachment 3) to the Western Australian Local Government Association regarding the proposed local government electoral reform with the following amendments:

  1. 2.1 - delete the statement “Council Recommendation: Support compulsory voting at Local Government elections”.
  1. 2.1 - add the statement that “Compulsory voting in conjunction with optional preferential voting, may lead to further politicisation of Local Government”. 
  1. Section 3 - include the entire WALGA position statement 2.5.2 verbatim, specifically adding points 3 and 4 which seek to allow more than one election service provider and for a mandated WAEC Report to Parliament.
  1. Section 3 – add that “Council does not support a full spill in 2027 to commence a four‑year election cycle rotation, as this approach would unfairly disadvantage Council members who have been duly elected to serve until 2029. Forcing these members to recontest their positions prematurely would not only undermine the mandate granted to them by the community but also impose unnecessary financial and personal burdens.”
  1. Section 3 Council Recommendation - add a specific reference requiring the WAEC to undertake comprehensive cost modelling so local governments can budget for the true cost of potential electoral reforms and clearly communicate to the community, the future costs to be borne by the ratepayer.
  1. Section 3 Council Recommendation – add a specific reference to implore the government to undertake community, sector wide consultation, prior to electoral reform draft legislation.
CARRIED 8/1
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Cicchini, Cr Grills, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Woods
Against:Cr Strutt

Reason for the Change
  • Point 1 serves to correct what appears to be an error.
  • Additional points serve to:
    • strengthen Councils position and rationale to support the status quo
    • request WAEC to conduct costs modelling 
    • implore the government to conduct community sector wide consultation to support the democratic process.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Emergency Services Annual Family Event 2026
I’d like to take a moment to recognise our volunteer bushfire brigades following the annual brigade BBQ held over the weekend. This event is a great opportunity to bring our volunteers together, thank them for their service, and strengthen the connections that keep our community safe.
Our brigades play a vital role across the Shire, responding to incidents, supporting preparedness, and giving their time so generously throughout the year. On behalf of Council, I’d like to thank every volunteer for the commitment, skill, and care they bring to protecting our community. Most importantly, I should note that Mt Helena Voluntary Bushfire Brigade were the proud winners of the Tug-of-War competition, a big congratulations!  

40th Anniversary Exhibition of the Shire of Mundaring Art Collection
I’d also like to acknowledge a special milestone for our arts community, with the 40th anniversary exhibition of the Shire of Mundaring Art Collection opened last Friday. The Marks of Mundaring exhibition celebrates four decades of creativity and showcases the talented artists who have helped shape the cultural identity of our community.
The collection reflects the unique character of the Perth Hills and highlights the important role arts and culture play in making the Shire of Mundaring a vibrant and connected place to live. It was wonderful to see the community come together to celebrate this achievement and the artists who continue to inspire us. The exhibition is open to view at the Mundaring Art Centre. 

Fraser Park Playground Upgrade and the Sculpture Park Improvements
We currently have community feedback open on both the Fraser Park playground upgrade and the Sculpture Park improvements, and I’d encourage anyone with an interest in these spaces to have their say.
These projects are great examples of how community input helps shape our local facilities, ensuring they reflect the needs and character of our community. We’ve already seen strong interest, and we’re keen to hear from as many residents as possible before designs are finalised.

Upcoming Shire Events
We also have a number of important events coming up across the Shire.
ANZAC Day services will be held across our local communities, providing an opportunity for us to come together, reflect, and honour those who have served our country.
We are also proud to be part of the 2026 WA Tree Festival, running from 11 April to 10 May. This month-long program celebrates the important role trees play in creating greener, healthier and cooler communities, and encourages everyone to get involved in protecting and growing our local canopy .
There are a range of ways to take part, including local workshops and opportunities to learn more about planting and caring for trees. At the Ordinary Council meeting held 10 March 2026 Ms Louise Stelfox of Darlington asked a question which was taken on notice. A written response was provided to Ms Stelfox, details of which are herewith.

Question 2
What is the Shire doing with the trees allocated under the Urban Canopy Grant Program and over the next four years, how will the Shire publicise the Treebate Program, which was announced in January 2025 to increase tree canopy in urban areas?

Response 2
Urban Canopy Grant Program
The Urban Canopy Grant Program has ceased and is no longer active. There are no remaining trees allocated to the Shire under this program.
 
The State Government’s current approach, led by the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development (DPIRD) and the Department of Water and Environmental Regulation (DWER), focuses on addressing tree canopy loss caused by the Polyphagous shot-hole borer (PSHB).
 
This includes the WA Tree Recovery Program, established in August 2024, which provides eligible residents with a rebate of up to $150 for replacement trees and associated planting items where trees have been removed under DPIRD authority. DWER has supported this program through community information kiosks across the metropolitan area. Further information is available on the WA Government website or via treerecovery@dwer.wa.gov.au .

Treebate Program
The Treebate Program is a State Government initiative administered by DWER to encourage native tree planting on private property and increase urban tree canopy.
 
Eligible Western Australians aged 18 years and over can claim a rebate of up to $150 for one eligible native tree, purchased from a local nursery, with claims submitted via the ServiceWA app. The program opened on 28 July 2025 and will operate for four years, supporting up to 10,000 rebates per year statewide.
 
While administered by the State Government, the Shire will promote the Treebate Program through its usual communication channels, as an example through the Six Seasons newsletters and by sharing State Government information as it becomes available.
 
Further information is available at: www.wa.gov.au/organisation/department-of-water-and-environmental-regulation/treebate 

 

Eric Smith, Glen Forrest
At the Ordinary Council meeting held 10 March 2026 Mr Eric Smith of Glen Forrest asked a question which was taken on notice. A written response was provided to Mr Smith, details of which are herewith.

Question 1
In reference to tonight's agenda - Decision 16, AEM 17-2-2026 in reference to LED signs, we keep getting fobbed off with an LED sign at the front of this administration building to tell the community what's going on. Could Council please supply in writing the MRWA reasoning for the decision of not applying a position of an LED sign in front of or in proximity of the Mundaring Shire's Administration Centre?
 
Response 1
Main Roads WA (MRWA) has not been asked to assess a formal LED sign application for the Shire of Mundaring Administration Centre.
However, Shire staff have reviewed MRWA’s Policy and Assessment Guidelines for Digital and Static Advertising Signs. Based on these requirements, particularly those relating to safety, crash risk categories, visibility distances, and locations where digital signage is not supported, such as proximity to intersection, the Shire has determined that an application for an LED sign at this location would be highly unlikely to receive MRWA approval.
It was explained at a previous Council Meeting, that the LED sign could potentially be installed at this location provided it was set back far enough from the road. However, that would defeat the purpose trying to be achieve which would be having motorist being able to read the sign. 
For this reason, a formal submission to MRWA has not been made.

Debra Bishop, Save Perth Hills
At the Ordinary Council meeting held 10 March 2026 Ms Debra Bishop of Stoneville asked a question which was taken on notice. A written response was provided to Mr Smith, details of which are herewith.

Question 2
Why hasn't the Shire's website been updated to inform the community that Satterley is seeking to reopen its appeal case in the State Tribunal for proposed North Stoneville, which would further extend the decision that the community is waiting for, and given the Shire has known about the reopening submission by Satterley since February 13?
 
Response 2
The Shire acknowledges that the information regarding Satterley’s request to reopen its appeal case in the State Administrative Tribunal for the proposed North Stoneville development was not updated on the website in a timely manner. This was an oversight. However, this has now been rectified and the relevant information is available for the community on our website: www.mundaring.wa.gov.au/plan-build/planning-scheme-maps-and-policies/north-stoneville-townsite.aspx

OFFICER RECOMMENDATION

That Council endorse the proposed amendments to the Brown Park Masterplan as per Attachment 1, specifically the relocation of the Skate Park, Public Toilet Block and the Pump/Jump Track, on the basis of:
  

  1. Identified site constraints, including physical, environmental and spatial limitations that affect the feasibility and long‑term functionality of the facilities in their current location;

  2. Additional community and stakeholder feedback, which has highlighted concerns regarding amenity, safety, accessibility, and the integration of youth recreation facilities within the broader precinct; and

  3. The recognised Aboriginal cultural heritage values associated with Woodbridge Creek, and preference to landscape the area in a manner that reflects and respects its cultural significance.

 

MOTION  
Moved by:Cr Mehta
Seconded by:Cr Woods

That Council endorse the proposed amendments to the Brown Park Masterplan as per Attachment 1, specifically the relocation of the Skate Park, Public Toilet Block and the Pump/Jump Track, on the basis of:
  

  1. Identified site constraints, including physical, environmental and spatial limitations that affect the feasibility and long‑term functionality of the facilities in their current location;

  2. Additional community and stakeholder feedback, which has highlighted concerns regarding amenity, safety, accessibility, and the integration of youth recreation facilities within the broader precinct; and

  3. The recognised Aboriginal cultural heritage values associated with Woodbridge Creek, and preference to landscape the area in a manner that reflects and respects its cultural significance.

  4. Acknowledgement that decisions around funding of the various elements in the master plan (including funded and/or unfunded elements) will be made by Council as part of annual Council Plan (Corporate Business Plan) long term financial plan and annual budget reviews.



AMENDMENT TO THE MOTION C-6-4-2026 
Moved by:Pres McNeil
Seconded by:Cr Heptinstall
Add the word "unfunded" before Pump/Jump Track in the first sentence. 
CARRIED 9/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Grills, Cr Cicchini, Cr Woods, Cr Strutt
Against:None

7.31PM – Point of Order
Cr Mehta raised a point of order during debate in accordance with the Shire of Mundaring Meeting Procedure Local Law 2015, Section 7.2(1)(a) whereby Cr Mehta believed statements made by Cr Cicchini were not relevant.  After clarification by Cr Cicchini, Pres McNeil agreed that Cr Cicchini’s comments were relevant to debate and the Point of Order was not upheld.

MOTION  
Moved by:Cr Mehta
Seconded by:Cr Woods

That Council endorse the proposed amendments to the Brown Park Masterplan as per Attachment 1, specifically the relocation of the Skate Park, Public Toilet Block and the unfunded Pump/Jump Track, on the basis of:
  

  1. Identified site constraints, including physical, environmental and spatial limitations that affect the feasibility and long‑term functionality of the facilities in their current location;

  2. Additional community and stakeholder feedback, which has highlighted concerns regarding amenity, safety, accessibility, and the integration of youth recreation facilities within the broader precinct; 

  3. The recognised Aboriginal cultural heritage values associated with Woodbridge Creek, and preference to landscape the area in a manner that reflects and respects its cultural significance; and

  4. Acknowledgement that decisions around funding of the various elements in the master plan (including funded and/or unfunded elements) will be made by Council as part of annual Council Plan (Corporate Business Plan) long term financial plan and annual budget reviews.


7:51pm meeting adjourned.

OFFICER RECOMMENDATION
Moved by:Cr Daw
Seconded by:Cr Grills
That Council:
  1. Notes the feedback from the Shire’s Environmental Advisory Group on the WALGA Climate Change Advocacy Position Consultation Paper (Attachment 1) indicating strong support for the draft advocacy position statement and the potential benefit to include the following two points:
    1. The issue regarding increasingly hot and dry summer months (due to climate change) and the related requirement to ensure continuity of mainstream power supply for domestic, business and essential services; and
    2. The onerous nature of financial costs on residents to provide their own emergency power supply systems; and
  2. Provides feedback to WALGA on the Climate Change Advocacy Position Consultation Paper, endorsing the draft advocacy position statement as follows, with consideration to add the two points raised by the Shire’s Environmental Advisory Group;
  1. Local Government acknowledges the risks associated with, and is committed to, addressing climate change. 
  2. WALGA calls on the Australian and Western Australian Governments to:
  1. Provide the necessary climate leadership, coordination and action to ensure an orderly transition to achieve emission reduction targets and address the impacts of climate change. 
  2. Provide dedicated funding, guidance and practical support to assist Local Governments to undertake emissions reduction and adaptation actions.

 

AMENDMENT TO THE MOTION C-10-4-2026 
Moved by:Cr Mehta
Seconded by:Cr Grills
  1. Include a further two points from Council for WALGA’s consideration being;
  1. Investment in reliable and climate-resilient energy infrastructure to ensure continuity of supply; and
  2. Equitable funding mechanisms to support households and communities in accessing affordable energy resilience solutions.
CARRIED 9/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Grills, Cr Cicchini, Cr Woods, Cr Strutt
Against:None
 
AMENDMENT TO THE MOTION C-11-4-2026 
Moved by:Cr Ellery
Seconded by:Cr Mehta
Include a further point from Council for WALGA’s consideration being;
c. Adaptation mechanisms should support households with non-reticulated water supply.
CARRIED 9/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Grills, Cr Cicchini, Cr Woods, Cr Strutt
Against:None

  

RESOLUTION NUMBER:C-12-4-2026

  1. The issue regarding increasingly hot and dry summer months (due to climate change) and the related requirement to ensure continuity of mainstream power supply for domestic, business and essential services; and
  2. The onerous nature of financial costs on residents to provide their own emergency power supply systems; 
  1. Provides feedback to WALGA on the Climate Change Advocacy Position Consultation Paper, endorsing the draft advocacy position statement as follows, with consideration to add the two points raised by the Shire’s Environmental Advisory Group;
  1. Local Government acknowledges the risks associated with, and is committed to, addressing climate change. 
  2. WALGA calls on the Australian and Western Australian Governments to:
  1. Provide the necessary climate leadership, coordination and action to ensure an orderly transition to achieve emission reduction targets and address the impacts of climate change. 
  2. Provide dedicated funding, guidance and practical support to assist Local Governments to undertake emissions reduction and adaptation actions; and
  1. Include a further three points from Council for WALGA’s consideration being;
  1. Investment in reliable and climate-resilient energy infrastructure to ensure continuity of supply; 
  2. Equitable funding mechanisms to support households and communities in accessing affordable energy resilience solutions; and
  3. Adaptation mechanisms should support households with non-reticulated water supply. 
CARRIED 8/1
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Grills, Cr Woods, Cr Strutt
Against:Cr Cicchini

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Gold Waterwise Council

I’m pleased to advise that the Shire of Mundaring has been re-endorsed as a Gold Waterwise Council in recognition of our continued dedication to sustainable water management and commitment to building waterwise communities over the 2024-2025 reporting year. 

Congratulations to Chloe Ironmonger and Jolene Quinn from our environment and sustainability team for their work.
Shire of Mundaring was commended on the introduction of sustainability being a required consideration in all Shire purchasing decisions, a Waterwise tactic to maintain local biodiversity. Our proactive approach to stormwater management, maintenance and improvement was also highlighted as a commendable approach to Water Sensitive Urban Design. 

We’re proud to see this work recognised and thank our team for their continued commitment to making Mundaring a Waterwise council."

30th Anniversary Mundaring Firefighters School

This year marks the 30th anniversary of the Mundaring Firefighters School, which has played an important role in training and supporting firefighters from across Western Australia. On behalf of Council and our community, I’d like to thank the many volunteers, trainers and emergency services personnel who have contributed to its success over the past three decades and helped strengthen emergency preparedness across our region.

Restricted Burning Period

I’d also like to remind residents that we remain in the Restricted Burning Period until 31 May. As we move further into the cooler months, it’s important that everyone continues to follow permit requirements and local fire safety regulations to help protect our community and environment.

Mother's Day

And finally, I’d like to extend a belated Happy Mother’s Day to all mothers, grandmothers, carers and mother figures across our community. Summary of Questions
Summary of Response
Debra Bishop - Save Perth Hills
1As we anticipate a decision from SAT is imminent, will the CEO write a formal letter to DPLH and WAPC reinforcing Council's position opposing urban development at North Stoneville and its 2020 MRS amendment request to rezone the North Stoneville land from urban to rural and seek the status of the proposed review of urban zoned land in the hills which, was part of that application to the Planning Commission?The Chief Executive Officer advised that the Shire is currently seeking clarification from the Department regarding its awareness of, and position on, the proposed rezoning. In terms of formal process, Council, together with Save Perth Hills, lodged independent submissions with the Department in 2021 requesting that the land be rezoned. That official request remains pending, subject to several requirements that the Western Australian Planning Commission referred back to the Department. Once the Shire has contacted the Department and received clarification, and if it becomes evident that the Department is either unaware of the rezoning request or is not progressing it, the Shire will formally submit a written request for the process to be reinitiated, should that be necessary.
2Will you be able to cc Save Perth Hills into that correspondence or provide a copy to Save Perth Hills to be able to share with the community?The Chief Executive Officer advised that if the Shire was to formally seek clarification in writing, a copy of the correspondence could be provided to Save Perth Hills.
Eric Smith - Glen Forrest
1Is the $196,000 storage facility in Farrell Road, Midvale which has been vacant for some time, what is currently happening as there appears to be no activity occuring? Or is it just a facility that we have developed as an expensive facility of ratepayer income?
Director Built & Natural Environment advised that the Shire does use the facility from time to time if works are being carried out in that part of the Shire.  Due to the space at the facility, the Shire also has a lease agreement with the charity group, Bicycles for Humanity, who utilise the space also.
2Why are we hot mixing small roads lines and cul-de-sacs that use little amounts of traffic instead of hot mixing thoroughfares that carry large amounts of traffic as many roads that do carry substantial amounts of traffic have been done or are partially done?
Director Built & Natural Environment advised that the Shire carries out roadworks based on road condition assessments with traffic volumes a consideration.  Quite a number of the Shire's heavy traffic roads have been ungraded over at least the past 20 years.
3Where are we at with the borrowing of money and what is the current and future debt that the Shire is up for? Considering that we are currently repaying around $90,000 per month to date and are we contemplating borrowing large amounts for future years that will lock our ratepayers in for future years to come and what will these borrowings be if approved by our Councillors?
The Director of Corporate Services advised that the Shire currently has two loans, which Mr Smith is referring to. One of these loans will mature in the next financial year. The second loan is scheduled to mature in the 2031/32 financial year. The Shire will continue to meet its repayment obligations until those maturities.
The Shire’s Long Term Financial Plan does not currently include any provision for new borrowings. However, this position is reviewed as part of the annual budget process and may change subject to Council’s future budget considerations.
The Shire President confirmed the two loans are for the construction of Mundaring Arena and the Boyal Community Centre.
4Because of the current fuel and financial situation that the community is in, will Councillors consider a nil rate increase and staff use restraint in requiring infrastructure demands including vehicle and equipment replacement?
The Chief Executive Officer advised that, at this point, Council is anticipating an increase in rates. When considering each financial year, decisions are made in the context of the Shire's Long Term Financial plan, therefore, the Shire is very reticent to make decisions based purely on what is happening at a particular point in time.  The Shire certainly does understand the financial strains in our community which are similar right across the state and across Australia and certainly the Shire are showing or implementing as much restraint as possible with respect to the projects currently being undertaken operationally and will continue to put as much downward pressure on operating expenditures as possible. However, at this stage again based on the long term financial planning, it is not realistic to expect the Council will have a nil rate increase this year.

OFFICER RECOMMENDATION/MOTION
That Council endorse the draft Western Australian Local Government Association's submission to the Western Australian State Government on recommended amendments to the Cat Act 2011.

RESOLUTION NUMBER: C-5-5-2026
MOTION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Ellery
Seconded by:Cr Mehta
That Council notes the draft Western Australian Local Government Association's submission to the Western Australian State Government on recommended amendments to the Cat Act 2011 and requests the CEO provide the following feedback:

  1. That Council recognises there may be some benefits of greater consistency between the Cat and Dog Acts but does not support the amalgamation of these if it causes further delays to the Cat Act Amendments;
  2. That Council's own Keeping of Cat Local Law requires permits for 3 or more cats and provisions for Fauna Protection Buffer Zones and does not wish for this autonomy to be ceded for consistency; and
  3. Council will be providing its own submission to DLGIRS given the short timeframes for feedback provided by WALGA.

CARRIED 9/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Grills, Cr Cicchini, Cr Woods, Cr Strutt
Against:None

The Chief Executive Officer has power to sub-delegate under DA05, DA34 and DA35.

    2. clarifying cross‑cutting and enterprise‑level risks; and
    3. supporting informed decision‑making by Council and the Audit, Risk and Improvement Committee.

Before commencing tonight's meeting, I would like to acknowledge several important contributions and achievements within our community.
 
King's Birthday Honours
I would like to congratulate former Shire of Mundaring Councillor Colin James and local resident Emeritus Professor Mark Bush, who have both been recognised in the 2026 King's Birthday Honours.

Mr James has been awarded the Australia Fire Service Medal in recognition of more than 40 years of dedicated volunteer service to emergency management and community safety.

He began volunteering with the Darlington Bush Fire Brigade in 1980 and has since served in numerous leadership roles. He has also supported major incidents across Western Australia and interstate through the Department of Fire and Emergency Services Air Operations Team and has spent decades helping local residents prepare for bushfire.
 
Professor Bush has been appointed a Member of the Order of Australia for significant service to engineering, tertiary education and the community.

Alongside a distinguished career in engineering and academia, Professor Bush has also made a valuable contribution to our community through his long-standing involvement with the Parkerville Volunteer Bushfire Brigade and serval terms as Captain. 

On behalf of Council and our community, I congratulate Colin and Mark on these well-deserved recognition honours and thank them both for their outstanding contribution over many years’ service.
 
Megan Griffiths
I would also like to acknowledge Director Place and Community, Megan Griffiths (who will be leaving the Shire of Mundaring in coming months). 

Megan has dedicated 18 years of service to the organisation and our community, making a significant contribution across a range of roles. Most recently, she has led the Place and Community Directorate through a period of growth and change with professionalism, commitment and strong leadership.

On behalf of Council, I sincerely thank Megan for her service and contribution to our community and wish her every success for the future.

 

Elsie Austin Invite
I would also like to invite our community to attend the official opening of the Elsie Austin Pavilion and Changerooms redevelopment at Mount Helena on Sunday, 5 July.

This important project has delivered modern facilities that will support local sporting clubs, volunteers and the broader community for years to come.

Funded through a partnership between Shire of Mundaring and the State Government through the PlayOnWA initiative, the redevelopment reflects a shared commitment to supporting active and connected communities.

I encourage residents to come along at 9am on Sunday 5 July to celebrate this important milestone for Mount Helena and our wider community.
 
National Reconciliation Week 
I would like to acknowledge National Reconciliation Week, which was recently celebrated across our community.

I thank the many Elders, community members, volunteers and organisations who participated in local events and activities, creating opportunities for learning, connection and understanding.

Shire of Mundaring remains committed to fostering respect, understanding and stronger relationships within our community.
 
Closing Remarks
Finally, I would like to acknowledge the many volunteers, community groups, emergency services personnel and residents who continue to make our community such a special place to live.

Summary of Response
John Bell, Mount Helena
1Related to Item 10.1 – Could you please explain why the focus of the limited strategy appears to have been pre-determined in the scope of work given to the consultants?
The CEO advised that the scope of work associated with the item was primarily focused on identifying how the Shire could achieve growth targets set by the Western Australian Government. It was noted that the current body of work has a strong emphasis on urban areas and potential urban expansion.
The CEO acknowledged that there may have been some confusion within the community regarding the scope. However, it was clarified that future stages of the Local Planning Strategy and Scheme review process will provide opportunities to consider rural residential and rural areas in more detail.
2Related to Item 10.1 – May I respectfully request a copy of the scope of work provided to the consultant?
The CEO confirmed that the Shire will provide a copy of the scope of work. 
Louise Stelfox, Darlington 
1The Shire officer’s proposed actions exclude direct communication with stakeholders, and no attendance of Shire officers at ratepayer meetings. At the Annual Electors Meeting of 2 February 2026, I raised a Motion emphasising the importance of the Shire’s engagement, partnership and collaboration with ratepayer groups for its community consultation to develop the Land Use Planning Strategy, Local Planning Strategy and Local Planning Scheme (No. 5). This Motion was passed unanimously, yet the Shire officer’s proposed actions exclude direct communication with stakeholders and there is no proposed attendance of Shire officers at ratepayer meetings. Why have Shire officers ignored my Motion in favour of the Shire’s Community Engagement Policy (CD-04), which is four years old?
The CEO advised that consultation details are outlined within the body of the report and do not exclude or preclude engagement with stakeholder or ratepayer groups.
It was noted that the consultation section identifies key stakeholders to be consulted, which include resident and ratepayer groups. The CEO emphasised the Shire’s commitment to undertaking broad and inclusive consultation in relation to the item, as well as throughout the development of the Local Planning Strategy and Scheme.
2The draft Land Use Planning Strategy report contains a number of typographical errors. How much was the ‘urban’ consultant, Niche Studio, paid for this draft?
The CEO advised that Niche Studio was paid approximately $60,000 to prepare the body of work.
In relation to the typographical errors, the CEO advised that staff have undertaken a detailed review of the document and identified approximately 10 typographical errors across the 65-page report. These errors are to be corrected prior to the document being released for community consultation.
Eric Smith, Glen Forrest
1With the development of the Mundaring Precinct Plan, where does the Mundaring War Memorial fit into the project? This would need to include the rose gardens, one of which runs north–south including the memorial as an “A” Class reserve, and the other along Great Eastern Highway, which is not an “A” Class reserve. Further consultation is required on whether the memorial is going to remain in its current location or be included in this multi-million dollar precinct plan.
The CEO advised that there are currently no plans to relocate the Mundaring War Memorial.
It was noted that the project remains at a high-level precinct design stage. The CEO further advised that if any future consideration were given to relocating the memorial, this would be subject to extensive and widespread community consultation prior to any decisions being made.
2It is rumoured that there have been many changes to this project, and it appears that the community has not been advised of these changes from the original concept presented some time ago. Where are we at with this situation?
The Shire President advised that a Special Council Meeting will be held on Wednesday, 17 June 2026 at 6:30pm in the Council Chamber to present the concept plan and business case for the Mundaring Cultural Hub.
The CEO advised that extensive community consultation has already occurred in relation to the project. This has included the establishment of a Community Reference Group, which has provided input throughout the lifecycle of the project.
It was noted that the project has now progressed to a stage where the concept design is largely finalised, and the business case is being completed for presentation to Council for consideration and potential endorsement to proceed.
Owen Briffa, Mount Helena
1Following on from the previous question regarding the Mundaring War Memorial, a meeting was held last Friday between myself, Eric Smith, Adam Hort and Shire President Paige McNeil. From that meeting, we would like to know whether the Mundaring War Memorial could be considered as the main entrance statement for the new Cultural Hub, instead of commissioned artwork at the entrance?
Taken on notice.
Louise Stelfox, Darlington
3Community information drop-in days are just that - information days. 
Imparting information is not consultation, and words matter. Currently, there is no transparency around how Shire officers will capture and incorporate stakeholder responses into the Land Use Planning Strategy (LUPS). 
Will Shire officers record each stakeholder’s comments and incorporate these into a report for consideration by Council following the Shire’s community consultation?
The CEO advised that drop-in sessions are designed to provide flexible opportunities for community members to attend across a range of times, improving accessibility.
It was noted that officers facilitating these sessions are responsible for recording key feedback received. This information is then compiled into a consolidated report.
The CEO further advised that the report presented to Council will include the issues and opportunities identified through consultation, along with a corresponding response from staff.
Eric Smith, Glen Forrest
3Where are we at with the Mundaring Precinct Plan project at this point in time? What is the cost to date, what is the anticipated cost of the finished project, and will Council be borrowing additional funds, noting that $15 million has already been allocated?
The Shire President advised that the project has funding of $15 million, in addition to $15 million received from the Federal Government.
The CEO advised that the project has progressed to the detailed conceptual design stage. It was noted that Council has set a project budget cap of $32 million, which is guiding the development of the project.
The CEO further advised that, as the project progresses, more detailed cost analysis will be available. At this stage, there are no plans for the Shire to undertake additional borrowings for the project.
The Shire President reiterated that Council has been clear in maintaining the budget cap, noting that earlier concept designs exceeded the budget and were subsequently scaled back to align with financial constraints.
4What is going to happen to all the other buildings of which many are of historical importance?
Will they be destroyed, demolished, sold off or relocated to an historical village area for posterity purposes?
The CEO advised that there are currently no plans to demolish or relocate the existing Visitor Centre or Arts Centre buildings in Mundaring.
It was noted that a body of work is being undertaken to explore potential retail or commercial opportunities within the precinct, with the intention to repurpose these buildings.
The CEO further advised that the existing library building, which is near the end of its useful life, is proposed for relocation. While no final decision has been made, the intent is that the current library building may be demolished and the site utilised for retail or other community purposes.
5It has been interesting reading the qualifications of the leading staff members and the expertise of the 4 heads of Mundaring shire on the Shires website.
Of all the years that these staff members have service in their appropriate areas have they, over the years, endeavoured to further and keep up to date advances and changes in this dynamic and fast changing world including updating qualifications?
The CEO advised that professional development is a key component of organisational practice. As part of the annual performance review process, discussions are held with Directors regarding professional development opportunities.
It was noted that, in addition to formal training, a range of internal learning and development initiatives are undertaken to build staff capability in priority areas.
The CEO further advised that his own professional development is reviewed annually by Council as part of the CEO performance review process.

COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION
That Council: 
  1. Adopts the draft Community Leases Policy, as attached to this report (Attachment 1); and
  2. Adopts the draft Appendix 2 - Community Leases Policy - Community Leases Guidelines, as attached to this report (Attachment 2). 

RESOLUTION NUMBER:C-10-6-2026 
MOTION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Pres McNeil
Seconded by:Cr Mehta
That Council: 
  1. Refers the draft Community Leases Policy, back to the Governance Committee for further consideration on the proposed changes to 4.3.1 - determining Market Rent.

CARRIED 8/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Grills, Cr Cicchini, Cr Woods, Cr Strutt
Against:None

Reason for Change
The proposed amendment to clause 4.3.1 that uses 'turnover' as the determinant for discounted market rent eligibility, for Not-for-Profit entities (Category 2) requires further consideration. While turnover is an objective measure, it doesn't reflect the financial realities of many not-for-profit community service organisations.
 
Some Not for Profits may exceed the proposed $500,000 turnover threshold, yet operate on a slim profit margin due to the high cost of wages inherent in delivering community services like childcare and aged care. Under the previous model, the 50% market rent discount enabled these organisations to budget surplus funds for government mandated wage increases and reinvest modest profits back into the organisation to ensure workforce sustainability and positive community outcomes. Relying on turnover alone risks disadvantaging our community service that provide much needed services to our community.

OFFICER RECOMMENDATION / MOTION
Moved by:                                      Cr Ellery
Seconded by:                                 Cr Mehta
That Council:
  1. Endorse the Mundaring Cultural Hub Concept Design pack, noting that minor refinement may be required through detailed design and further value engineering;
  2. Endorse the Mundaring Cultural Hub external facade concept as presented, noting the colour theme of "Ivory Terracotta";
  3. Endorse the Mundaring Cultural Hub Business Case;
  4. Approve the commencement of the procurement activity for the construction of the Mundaring Cultural Hub, with an Expression of Interest process to shortlist competent contractors followed by a Request for Tender process; and
  5. Note that the Request for Tender submissions for a construction contract are scheduled to be presented to Council for consideration and award at the December 2026 Ordinary Council Meeting.

OFFICER RECOMMENDATION
Moved by:Cr Mehta
Seconded by:Cr Heptinstall
That Council:
  1. Accepts the offer received for the purchase of 2-4 Scott Street, Greenmount, subject to compliance with the local public notice requirements of section 3.58 of the Local Government Act 1995;
  2. Notes that should any submissions be received during the public notice period that do not support the sale, a further report will be presented to Council for consideration prior to finalising the disposal; and 
  3. Authorises the CEO to give public notice in accordance with section 3.58, and to finalise and execute all necessary documentation to give effect to the disposal subject to no public submissions that do not support the sale being received. 

For:None
Against:None

6.05PM – Point of Order
Cr Mehta raised a point of order during debate in accordance with the Shire of Mundaring Meeting Procedure Local Law 2015, Section 7.2(1)(a) whereby Cr Mehta believed statements made by Cr Grills were not relevant.  After clarification by the Chief Executive Officer, President McNeil agreed that Cr Grills comments were relevant to debate and the Point of Order was not upheld.

 

RESOLUTION NUMBER:SC-4-6-2026 
AMENDMENT TO THE MOTION 
Moved by:Cr Ellery
Seconded by:Cr Mehta
That Council adds an additional point being:
  1. Makes the sale of the 2-4 Scott Street subject to confirmation that Main Roads WA do not require the land for their proposed Scott St / Great Eastern Highway intersection safety improvement works. 
CARRIED 8/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Grills, Cr Woods, Cr Strutt
Against:None

THE AMENDMENT WAS CARRIED

RESOLUTION NUMBER:SC-5-6-2026

OFFICER RECOMMENDATION/MOTION
That Council approves the development application for the proposed Tourist and Visitor Accommodation at No.3-5 (Lot 102) The Crescent, Helena Valley subject to the following conditions:

  1. This planning approval is only for Tourist and Visitor Accommodation as defined by Local Planning Scheme No. 4 and shown on the approved plans. 
  2. The development shall comply with the approved plans (including any amendments marked in red) unless approval is granted by the Shire for any minor variation made necessary by detailed design. 
  3. The development shall comply with the approved Property Management Plan prepared by Gonzalo Sepulveda dated 12 February 2026 to the satisfaction of the Shire. 
  4. The development shall comply with the Environmental Protection (Noise) Regulations 1997 to the satisfaction of the Shire. 
  5. No more than 8 guests are to be on site at any one time to the satisfaction of the Shire. 
  6. No amplified music is permitted on site to the satisfaction of the Shire. 
  7. Prior to commencement of the use, the mitigation measures recommended in the approved Acoustic Noise Management Plan (prepared by Acoustic Engineering Solutions and dated 10 February 2026) shall be implemented, with certification provided to the Shire and thereafter complied with by the landowner(s) for the life of the development to the satisfaction of the Shire. 
  8. An application to install an on-site effluent disposal system must be submitted with the application for a building permit. The Tourist and Visitor Accommodation shall be connected to the approved on-site effluent disposal system installed to the satisfaction of the Shires Health Service, prior to occupancy. 
  9. Prior to applying for a building permit, a lighting plan prepared by a suitably qualified consultant/engineer shall be submitted to the Shire for approval. The plan shall include measures to minimise light spill onto adjoining residential land and have due regard to Australian Standard 4282 (as amended). Lighting and lighting infrastructure shall thereafter be established and maintained in accordance with the approved lighting plan, to the satisfaction of the Shire. 
  10. All stormwater must be managed onsite to prevent erosion and transportation of water borne pollutants, to the satisfaction of the Shire. 
  11. The development shall comply with the Bushfire Management Plan prepared by Bushfire Prone Planning dated 14 January 2026 to the satisfaction of the Shire. 
  12. Prior to commencement of use, information is to be provided to demonstrate that the measures contained in Section 4 of the bushfire management plan by Bushfire Prone Planning dated 14 January 2026 have been implemented to the satisfaction of the Shire. This information should include a completed 'Certification by Bushfire Consultant' from the bushfire management plan. 
  13. The Asset Protection Zone shall be established prior to construction and the property thereafter maintained in accordance with the Bushfire Management Plan approved by the Shire. 
  14. Significant trees (such as habitat trees) have been identified onsite and in the Bushfire Management Plan/Statement/Site Plan for retention and protection. Measures to protect significant trees during construction works shall include Tree Protection Zones (TPZs) in accordance with AS 4970-2007. Protection of trees on development sites require the TPZs to be fenced, creating a physical barrier from construction impacts. 
  15. All native vegetation on the lot shall be retained unless clearing is specifically exempt under the Local Planning Scheme No 4 or required under an approved Bushfire Management Plan or Statement. 
  16. Prior to applying for a building permit, a Basic Dieback Management Plan shall be submitted for approval by the Shire to identify appropriate management practices for preventing the spread of Phytophthora dieback. The site works shall be undertaken in accordance with the recommendations in the approved dieback management plan. 
  17. Prior to applying for a building permit, engineering drawings and specifications detailing the construction and drainage of the car park and vehicle access shall be submitted to the satisfaction of the Shire. The car park and vehicle access shall thereafter be constructed in accordance with the approved plans. 
  18. Prior to commencement of use, 7 car parking bays and the manoeuvring/circulation areas shown on the approved plans shall be sealed/paved, surface marked in accordance with Australian Standard 2890.1 - Off-street car parking and Australian Standard 2890.6 - Off-street parking for people with disabilities (where relevant), kerbed and drained and thereafter maintained by the landowner(s) for the life of the development to the satisfaction of the Shire. 
  19. Prior to occupation the applicant shall submit an advertising signage plan to the Shire for approval and such signage maintained for the life of the development to the satisfaction of the Shire. 

RESOLUTION NUMBER:C-5-7-2026

Seconded by:Cr Woods

CARRIED 6/0

    • Firewood shall not be supplied or made available for use during any period in which campfires or solid-fuel fires are prohibited by DFES. 
    • Signage will be installed adjacent to the fire pit, clearly identifying any restrictions on use and advising guests when operation of the fire pit is prohibited. 
    • Guests must obtain prior approval from the property manager, host, or authorised staff member before using the fire pit. 
    • Written bushfire safety information, including fire pit operating requirements and restrictions, will be provided within each accommodation unit and made available to all guests upon arrival.

    • Where fire pit use is prohibited due to fire weather conditions, fire bans, or emergency warnings, guests will be notified promptly via SMS and/or other appropriate communication methods. The fire pit will be closed and clearly signed as unavailable for use during the restricted period.

OFFICER RECOMMENDATION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Woods
Seconded by:Cr Daw
That Council:
  1. Supports the Lake Leschenaultia Open Water Community Swim (40th Anniversary) under the Arts, Culture and Events Funding Program;
  2. Approve funding of $10,000 to Maida Vale Masters Swimming Club Inc under the Tier 3 – Activation Event;
  3. Require standard funding agreement conditions, including: 
    • Acknowledgement of the Shire’s support in all promotional materials
    • Post-event reporting on attendance, outcomes, and expenditure
  4. Provides in-kind support where appropriate; and 
  5. Requires post-event reporting on:
    • Attendance
    • Community outcomes 

CARRIED 6/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Cicchini, Cr Woods
Against:None

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Stronger Together Expo
This morning I had the pleasure of attending the Stronger Together Expo, which brought together local families and service providers focused on supporting wellbeing, resilience and community connection.
The event highlighted the wide range of services available to families across our community and provided valuable opportunities for people to connect with local organisations and support networks. It was particularly fitting that the Expo incorporated activities celebrating NAIDOC Week, giving families the opportunity to engage with and learn about Country through meaningful experiences.
Thank you to Midvale Hub, all participating organisations and the many community members who attended and helped make the event such a success.
 
Elsie Austin Reserve Changerooms
Last week we celebrated the official opening of the new Elsie Austin Reserve changeroom facility in Mount Helena. 
This important project provides modern, inclusive and accessible amenities that will support local sporting clubs, volunteers and families for many years to come. It is a wonderful example of what can be achieved when all levels of government work together with local sporting organisations to deliver facilities that meet the needs of a growing community.
 
Mundaring Cultural Hub
I am also pleased to advise that the Mundaring Cultural Hub project has reached another significant milestone.
Following Council's endorsement of the concept design, the project is now progressing to the tender phase, representing an important step towards delivery of this transformative community facility.

The Cultural Hub will create a vibrant new home for arts, culture, history, learning and tourism in the heart of Mundaring. It will bring together the Mundaring Arts Centre and Mundaring and Hills Historical Society alongside a contemporary library, visitor services and flexible community spaces.

Advocacy and Community Infrastructure
Advocacy remains an important responsibilities of local government leadership, and I have continued to work closely with State and Federal representatives to secure investment for our community.
On behalf of Council I recently, I met with Federal Ministers King and McBain, alongside Member for Bullwinkel Trish Cook, to discuss the future of Brown Park in Swan View.

Brown Park is home to more than 30 community user groups and significant improvements have already been delivered, including upgraded sporting infrastructure, lighting, parking and improved playing surfaces. Our next priority is securing funding for a new pavilion and changeroom facility that will provide modern, accessible amenities for the many clubs and community groups that call Brown Park home.
 
Parkerville Oval Lighting Upgrade
Works are now underway on the installation of new lighting at Parkerville Oval. 
This project has been strongly supported by the local community and will significantly improve access to sporting facilities for our junior and senior sporting teams.
 
Stoneville Road and Great Eastern Highway Safety Initiative
A near-miss monitoring camera has now been installed at the intersection of Stoneville Road and Great Eastern Highway. This initiative will collect important data to better understand safety risks at the intersection and support future advocacy and planning efforts.

Importantly, this is not an enforcement camera and does not issue fines. Its purpose is to gather evidence and improve road safety outcomes for our community.
I would like to thank Adam Hort MLA, the Member for Kalamunda, the WA Road Safety Commission and Shire officers for supporting this important initiative.

Summary of Questions
Summary of Response
Christian Jackson Stegner
1What are the purchaser's plans for the land at 2–4 Scott Street, Greenmount, and will it be used for infrastructure improvements to Scott Street?
The Council President advised that Council had considered the sale of the land at its previous meeting and that the resolution included a requirement to obtain confirmation from Main Roads that the land was not required for any future road upgrade works at the Scott Street intersection. The CEO further advised that the sale had not yet been finalised and discussions with the prospective purchaser were continuing. At this stage, it was understood that any future use of the site would likely involve a residential-based development, however any proposal would be subject to a future development application and assessment process. It was also confirmed that Main Roads had advised the subject land was not required for any future intersection improvement works.
2Is there any involvement of the CATS Group, which is involved in infrastructure and defence work, with this property?
The CEO advised that he was unable to provide any additional information beyond his previous response and had no further information to provide on the matter.
Eric Smith
1Why did the Shire purchase a new grader when the previous grader had been repaired, particularly when there is difficulty attracting an operator and the machine may remain idle?
The Director Built and Natural Environment advised that the Shire had recently lost its grader operator and recruitment was underway. The grader had been fully operational while an operator was in place. The Shire intended to continue operating the grader and would continue to review operational requirements and the potential use of contractors if necessary.
2The Shire appears to advertise a number of positions throughout the year. What are the concerns or issues regarding staffing in both administrative and works areas?
The CEO advised that the Shire's turnover rate was below industry average and currently under 20%. He noted that, as an organisation employing approximately 250–300 staff, it was normal to see a continual flow of recruitment activity. The CEO advised that available workforce data did not indicate any significant concerns regarding staff turnover.
Michael Salas 
1Is the proposal for tourist and visitor accommodation at 3–5 The Crescent, Helena Valley, 100% legal within the zoning provisions applying to the area?
The Manager Community Planning advised that the proposed land use could be considered under the provisions of Local Planning Scheme No. 4. The use is identified as an advertised land use, requiring public consultation before Council can determine whether it should be supported within the Residential zone.
2Can the maximum number of people who will be accommodated on the site at any one time be confirmed?
The Manager Community Planning advised that the applicant's report identified a maximum occupancy of approximately eight people on the site at any one time.
Daniel Booth
1To what extent were the submissions and objections received from neighbouring property owners considered in reaching the recommendation to support the proposed tourist accommodation development?
The Manager Community Planning advised that a Schedule of Submissions was included with the officer report and detailed both the submissions received and the officers’ responses. Following assessment of the proposal and submissions, officers formed the view that the development could be supported subject to a range of conditions and therefore recommended conditional approval.
2How has the safety and security of children and nearby residents been considered in the Shire's recommendation to support the proposal?
The Manager Community Planning advised that these matters had been considered through the assessment process and were addressed within the Operational Management Plan. It was noted that safety and security considerations were also discussed within the Schedule of Submissions attached to the report.
Eric Smith
3When will the decision relating to the Ford Blitz fire vehicle be revoked and reversed, and the vehicle returned to the Shire for relocation and display within the Shire of Mundaring?
The Shire President advised that the matter had been considered by the Bush Fire Advisory Committee, whose membership includes representatives from all Volunteer Bush Fire Brigades within the Shire. The Committee had unanimously supported the decision not to retain the vehicle within the Shire. 
The Director Built and Natural Environment advised that the vehicle was non-operational and that efforts to secure funding or identify a local group willing to undertake restoration had been unsuccessful. Following consultation, the vehicle had been offered to the Whiteman Park Motor Museum, which intended to restore and preserve it for historical display purposes.

RESOLUTION NUMBER: C-1-7-2026 
MOTION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Daw
Seconded by:Cr Cicchini
That in accordance with clause 4.3(13) of the Shire of Mundaring Meeting Procedures Local Law 2015 Public Question time be extended by a further 15 minutes. 
CARRIED 6/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Cicchini, Cr Woods
Against:None

Summary of Questions
Summary of Response
Garry Vitler
1How many residents were given the opportunity to object to or support the proposed tourist accommodation development at 3–5 The Crescent, Helena Valley?
The Manager Community Planning advised that 47 letters were distributed to nearby landowners as part of the public advertising process.
2If the development is approved and noise becomes an issue, what process is available to residents to have the matter addressed?The Manager Community Planning advised that the Operational Management Plan required contact details for the site manager to be provided to surrounding landowners. Residents would therefore be able to contact the site manager directly regarding concerns. In addition, the Noise Management Plan included mitigation measures, including proposed increases to boundary fencing, intended to minimise potential noise impacts.
Angus Booth
1How can the speed limit on Great Eastern Highway through Glen Forrest be reduced from 80 km/h to 60 km/h?
The Director Built and Natural Environment advised that speed limit assessments and approvals are undertaken by Main Roads Western Australia. Any request for a reduced speed limit would need to be assessed against Main Roads' criteria. It was noted that the speed limit through the area had previously been reduced from 90 km/h to 80 km/h.
2Given the needs of pedestrians, older people and people with disability, is it fair and appropriate for the speed limit through Glen Forrest to be reduced?
The Shire President reiterated that Great Eastern Highway falls under the jurisdiction of Main Roads Western Australia and that any decision to amend the speed limit would need to be made by that authority. While the Shire could advocate on behalf of the community, it did not have the power to make the change itself.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Petition 1 – Great Eastern Highway Speed Limit Reduction
A petition submitted by Mr Angus Taylor Booth requesting that Council seek a reduction in the speed limit on Great Eastern Highway, Glen Forrest from 80 km/h to 60 km/h from the existing speed reduction signage prior to Flint and Margaret Roads through to McGlew Road.
The petition cited road safety, pedestrian amenity and the protection of the residential and business precinct as reasons supporting the request.
The petition contained 2 signatures.

Petition 2 – Great Eastern Highway Truck Stop
A petition submitted by Mr Angus Taylor Booth requesting that Council advocate for the construction of a fully operational truck stop on the southern carriageway of Great Eastern Highway in Glen Forrest.
The petition cited support for the freight and transport industry, provision of driver rest facilities and potential economic benefits to local businesses as reasons supporting the request.
The petition contained 3 signatures.

 


RESOLUTION NUMBER:C-3-7-2026 
OFFICER RECOMMENDATION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Mehta
Seconded by:Cr Cicchini
That Council receive the petition submitted by Mr Booth and refer it to the Chief Executive Officer for action.
  1. Decrease the speed limit from 80 km/hr to 60 km/hr on Great Eastern Highway, Glen Forrest; and 
  2. Build and provide a fully operational truck-stop on the Southern carriageway side of Great Eastern Highway. 
CARRIED 6/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Cicchini, Cr Woods
Against:None

OFFICER RECOMMENDATION/MOTION
That Council endorse the Shire of Mundaring Advocacy Priority Areas as outlined in this report, to guide advocacy activities with State and Federal Government, sector agencies and key stakeholders.

  1. Housing, Aged Care / Retirement Living, Town Centre Revitalisation and Sustainable Growth
    1. Mundaring Town Centre development (including mixed use, higher density and aged care / independent living)
    2. Mundaring Wastewater Treatment Plant expansion
  2. Infrastructure and Connectivity
    1. Telecommunications
      1. Resilience in emergency (e.g. storm/bushfire)
      2. General connectivity (including satellite technology)
    2. Road Safety – Scott Street and Eastlink (watching brief, noting environmental impact concerns)
    3. Public transport in the foothills
  3. Community Resilience and Emergency Services Modernisation
    1. Volunteer brigades support (State Government capital funding gaps and operational funding gaps – through ESL)
    2. Disaster funding – seeking a review of the Federal Government guidelines on disaster funding (making it easier for Council to receive financial support)
  4. Healthy, Connected and Active Communities
    1. Brown Park development focus
    2. Helena River Parkland master planning
    3. Universal changerooms – per Council plan
    4. Mundaring Weir, seeking a review in providing greater community access including a review of State Agreements
    5. Reinstatement and expansion of funding for sporting facilities (CSRFF and/or Play on WA)

 

RESOLUTION NUMBER:C-11-7-2026

    2. Mundaring Wastewater Treatment Plant expansion

    1. Telecommunications
      1. Resilience in emergency (e.g. storm/bushfire)
      2. General connectivity (including satellite technology)
    2. Road Safety – Scott Street and Eastlink (watching brief, noting environmental impact concerns)
    3. Public transport in the foothills
  1. Community Resilience and Emergency Services Modernisation
    1. Volunteer brigades support (State Government capital funding gaps and operational funding gaps – through ESL)
    2. Disaster funding – seeking a review of the Federal Government guidelines on disaster funding (making it easier for Council to receive financial support)
  1. Healthy, Connected and Active Communities

CARRIED 6/0

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"I'd like to take a moment to congratulate Councillor Ben Heptinstall on his success at the 2026 Swan Chamber of Commerce and City of Swan Business Awards.
 
Many of us know Ben through his long-standing involvement in the Hills business community, where he has been a passionate advocate for local enterprise and economic development. His commitment to supporting businesses and strengthening our region has earned him widespread respect across the community.
 
I am delighted to share that Ben was awarded the People's Choice Award, a recognition that reflects the strong support and admiration he enjoys from those who know and work with him.
 
The Shire of Mundaring was also proud to be a sponsor of this year's awards, which celebrate the achievements, innovation and contribution of businesses across the region.
 
There were many Shire of Mundaring businesses that took out awards on Saturday.
