RESOLUTION NUMBER:SC-3-7-2026
MOTION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Heptinstall
Seconded by:Cr Mehta
That Council, by absolute majority, adopts:

  1. The following waste charges for the collection and disposal of waste in accordance with the provisions of the Waste Avoidance & Resources Recovery Act 2007:
  1. For residential properties with a bin collection service, a rubbish and waste service charge of $555.
  2. For residential properties with a 240L General Waste Bin swapped out in place of a 140L General Waste Bin, a charge of $105.
  3. For multi-unit residential properties with a shared bin collection service, a rubbish and waste service charge of $468.
  4. For non-rateable properties with a FOGO and General Waste Collection service, a rubbish and waste charge of $356.
  5. For non-rateable properties with a kerbside recycling, a charge of $96. 
  6. For non-rateable properties with a transfer station pass, a charge of $220.
  7. Any additional 140L General Waste Bin services, a charge of $131 per service.
  8. Any additional 240L General Waste Bin services, a charge of $236 per service.
  9. Any additional Recycling Bin services, a charge of $76 per service.  
  10. Any additional FOGO Bin services, a charge of $175 per service. 
  11. For commercial properties, a charge of $267 for a General Waste Bin serviced once a week.
  12. For commercial properties, a charge of $96 for a kerbside recycling service of once per fortnight.
  13. For commercial properties, a charge of $195 for a weekly FOGO collection service.
  14. For commercial properties, a charge of $1400 for a weekly bulk General Waste bin service (660 litres); and
  15. For commercial properties, a charge of $1200 for each additional lift for a weekly bulk General Waste bin service (660 litres); and
  1. The Annual Budget for the year ending 30 June 2027 as detailed in Attachment 1, incorporating but not limited to the following:
  1. A general rate of 7.0861 cents in the dollar of the Gross Rental Value to be levied on all rateable property within the Shire of Mundaring for the 2026/27 financial year. 
  2. A general rate of 0. 545 cents in the dollar to be levied on all Unimproved Value property within the Shire of Mundaring for the 2026/27 financial year.
  3. A minimum rate of $1059 for the 2026/27 financial year for Gross Rental Value Properties.
  4. A minimum rate of $1339 for the 2026/27 financial year for Unimproved Value Properties.
  5. The following dates being set for payment of rates by instalments and payment in full be approved:   
    1. Full payment or First instalment due date of 22 September 2026 or 35 days after the date of issue appearing on the rates notice, whichever is the later.
    2. Second instalment due date of 24 November 2026 or two months after the due date of the first instalment, whichever is the later.
    3. Third instalment due date of 18 February 2027 or two months after the due date of the second instalment, whichever is the later. 
    4. Fourth and final instalment due date of 22 April 2027 or two months after the due date of the third instalment, whichever is the later.
  6. An interest rate of 7% per annum payable on rates, or any instalment of a rates, that remains unpaid after it is due and payable.
  7. An interest rate of 11% per annum payable on the ESL charge, or any instalment of the ESL charge, that remains unpaid after it is due and payable.
  8. The interest rate of 7% per annum is not applied to unpaid rates for eligible pensioners, eligible seniors and deceased estates subject to probate.
  9. The maintaining of an overdraft facility of up to $500,000 and credit card facility of up to $56,000 for the purpose of providing a credit facility for normal Municipal Fund operational expenditure during the year. 
  10. The adoption of the following Elected Members Fees and Allowances for 2026/27:
    1. An annual allowance in lieu of meeting fees for elected members other than the Shire President of $26,931. 
    2. An annual allowance in lieu of meeting fees for the Shire President of $36,112. 
    3. An annual allowance for the Shire President of $73,435. 
    4. An annual allowance for the Deputy Shire President of $18,358; and 
    5. An Information and Communication Technology Allowance of $3,500 per Elected Member. 
  11. A per meeting fee of $465 for independent Audit, Risk and Improvement Committee members.  
  12. The 2026/27 Capital Works Program as detailed in the budget. 
  13. The Schedule of Fees and Charges for 2026/27 as detailed in the budget.
  1. As a result of the amendments to the recommended rate in the dollar and minimum rates for both Gross Rental Value and Unimproved Value properties, amend the budget as follows: 
  1. Decrease budgeted total rates revenue in 2026/27 by $198,907 to a revised amount of $37,541,486;
  2. Decrease budgeted employee costs for 2026/27 by $70,000 to a revised amount of $30,572,217; and
  3. Decrease budgeted materials and contracts costs for 2026/27 by $128,907 to a revised amount of $26,532,484.
CARRIED 9/0 BY ABSOLUTE MAJORITY
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Grills, Cr Cicchini, Cr Woods, Cr Strutt
Against:None

Reason for Change
The proposed 4.9% increase in gross rates yield (3.9% rate increase plus 1% growth in rate base) represents a slight decrease to the officer recommendation. MOTION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Ellery
Seconded by:Cr Mehta
That Council, in accordance with Schedule 2, Part 4, Clause 20(2) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, recommends that the Western Australian Planning Commission (WAPC) approves proposed Structure Plan 84 (refer Attachment 1), subject to the following modifications: 
  1. Modification of the Bushfire Management Plan (BMP), in accordance with advice received from the Department of Fire and Emergency Services (DFES), to address the following matters to the satisfaction of DFES and the Shire of Mundaring:
    1. Element 2 - Siting and Design: (A2.1 – Siting and design); and
    2. Element 3 - Vehicular Access (A3.3a – No-through roads); and
    3. Element 3 - Vehicular Access (A3.5a – Perimeter roads); and
    4. Element 4 - Water Supply (A4.1 – Water supply for structure plans); and 
  2. Modification of the Transport Impact Assessment (TIA), in accordance with advice received from Main Roads Western Australia (MRWA), to reflect the revised location and access arrangement to Helena Valley Road demonstrating the provision of auxiliary left-turn and right-turn treatments, to the satisfaction of MRWA and the Shire of Mundaring; and
  3. Modification of the Structure Plan Report (refer Attachment 1) to require that the detailed design of the road network, including the auxiliary left-turn and right-turn treatment and any associated carriageway widening, be undertaken to the satisfaction of Main Roads Western Australia and the Shire of Mundaring; and
  4. Modification of the Structure Plan Map (refer Attachment 2) to: 
    1. Remove all residential lots within the Western Power easement area, with the affected land and some adjacent land not impacted by easement to be utilised for Public Open Space;
    2. Reduction in density to R10 of lots adjoining Helena Valley road which may be offset by increase to R25 for other lots;
    3. Show all road reserves within the Structure Plan area being no less than 16 metres in width to accommodate new street tree planting in accordance with the Shire’s Street Trees Local Planning Policy (PS-08); 
    4. Identify and depict the auxiliary left-turn and right-turn treatments on Helena Valley Road into the Structure Plan area; and
    5. Address any other modifications rendered necessary in response to the modifications outlined within this recommendation.
  5. That Council requests the Chief Executive Officer write to the applicant requesting that, at the subdivision stage, the developer engage and collaborate with the Bibbul Ngarma Aboriginal Association in the preparation and finalisation of the Foreshore Management Plan.

CARRIED 7/2
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Ellery, Cr Grills, Cr Cicchini, Cr Woods, Cr Strutt
Against:Cr Daw, Cr Heptinstall

 

Reason for Change:
POS change is to support access and walkability to POS for the Southern development and ensure the space is usable for play equipment.

Change in R codes is to reduce the urban impact on the road reserves, which mitigates the loss of amenity for what was a previously agrarian entry to housing estates.

The letter is to ensure collaboration in the development of the foreshore and the master plans for the area being undertaken by Bibbul Ngarma Aboriginal On Sunday, the Shire of Mundaring hosted its first Dying to Know Expo, bringing together community members, presenters and exhibitors to explore end-of-life planning, grief and final wishes in a welcoming and supportive environment. It was wonderful to see so many people engaging openly with what can often be a difficult topic, and I thank everyone who attended, presented and volunteered to make the event such a success at our Boya Community Centre.

The Hills Talk Podcast Launch
I'm also pleased to announce the launch of The Hills Talk, the Shire's new monthly podcast celebrating the people, places and stories that make the Perth Hills such a special place to live. The podcast features conversations with local volunteers, community leaders, creatives, environmental advocates and others who help shape our wonderful community. Summary of Questions
Summary of Response
Ivan Selak, Swan View
1Helena Valley Road Bridge over Row Highway, barrier, cones, lights, 40km limit speed sign. When will these barriers be removed and made safe?The Director of Built and Natural Environment confirmed works are intended to involve a potential guard rail to improve the safety of the location, however Main Roads advised because there were some services they discovered that weren't in their original plans they have had to halt the works for now whilst they work out what they do next, they have temporarily left the work as it is. Director advised the Shire can follow up to see if it can be made safe in the meantime. The Shire President also confirmed this is a Main Roads project, not a Shire of Mundaring project.
2Fogo and smaller general red waste bins. Can we get a larger bin or can we go back to a fortnightly service?The Shire President noted this has been a long topic of debate and was a State Government directive. 
The Director of Built and Natural Environment advised yes, it is possible to upgrade to a 240L bin or purchase an addition 140L bin, there is a cost attached relating to the additional cost to landfill rather than the processing cost for the FOGO material which is cheaper.
The Shire President also advised there is a compassionate waste policy relating to people with additional medical waste can receive an upgrade or extra bin at no extra cost. If anyone is experiencing financial difficulty, we ask them to reach out to the Shire for a conversation. At this point in time, the Shire is following the State Governments waste strategy which introduced FOGO as a weekly collection and the red bin as a fortnightly collection.
Mariette Tanneau, Glen Forrest
1Retrospective planning approval granted for a deck on 6 Rachel Court, we are the adjourning neighbour. Why is the assessment ignoring the Planning Act for overlooking outdoor living spaces?The Manager Community Planning advised the criteria for visual privacy sits within the residential design codes. There is an ability to vary the minimum set back requirements in the event that it does meet the design principals. The Shire officers have been out on site and assessed that the deck in question is considered to meet the design principals and as such there has been conditional approval issued for the neighbouring deck.
2Why did the Shire not inform us of the planning process and approval from May. It took 3 emails in June and July to receive a little bit of information and we still do not have an approval date. We have no documentation, so if we want to object, how are we able to object as we have no information on this process?The Manager Community Planning advised in terms of the approval, the determination was only recently issued in the last 2 weeks. There was notice of determination provided by email, the Manager of Community Planning will follow up on this email. In terms of third-party appeal rights, unfortunately West Australian planning framework does not offer third-party appeal rights, so for an opportunity for a third-party to appeal there is no scope to do so unfortunately.
Phillip Graham, Helena Valley
1Boya Oval Upgrade - why was no one in Glenwood Avenue consulted? How many letters were handed out?The Director of Built and Natural Environment advised letters were sent out to residents of the area a number of weeks ago and our Community Engagement Officer has spoken to a number of residents as a result of that and has gone through what the plan entails and discussed any concerns that they had. Letters were sent to residents that back up to the Boya Oval plus ones along Glenwood Avenue. 
The Chief Executive Officer advised that the Shire will send a letter to Phillip and reach out directly to provide more information of the Boya Oval Upgrades and to seek his feedback.
Mariette Tanneau, Glen Forrest
3If it is deemed by Council to be an incorrect assessment, what can we do to correct the situation? If nothing can be done and we wish to maintain privacy will Council give us approval to erect our own screening on our property such as a shade sail? What is the process?The Manager Community Planning advised screening is at the discretion of the landowner. Based upon the Shires determination, it has been determined that there is an adequate separation to the neighbouring property’s outdoor areas of sensitivity when it does come to visual privacy assessment. Having been out on site it was noted there is about a 35m proximity difference between the deck as well as the area in question. In terms of any further screening, it would be at the discretion of that landowner. If the neighbouring property wanted to install screening materials that would be looking at impeding the visual aspects or intrusion as per what has been advised tonight, they are welcome to do so and alternatively there may be a conversation that could be had between the neighbouring landowners in order to provide above and beyond screening to what has already been installed on the decking area. The Shire President advised that the Manager Community Planning will be in further contact.

1Kerbside Collection. When did council become aware that it wasn't going to take place on schedule and what will happen with already placed bulk waste on the verge?
The Chief Executive Officer advised the Shire acknowledges there was an error in communication with council members and the community.  Individual Council members were not aware of these issues until the community were advised. Only one tender was received and unfortunately, they couldn't provide the services within necessary timeframe. 
Shire staff worked to identify an alternate option for a clear pathway forward. The Shire acknowledges we should have identified that this service wasn't going to happen a month prior.  Messages will go to community tomorrow, noting green waste collections are commencing from 18th August. The Chief Executive Officer advised that the green waste was given a priority as we move into the bush fire season. 
The Chief Executive Officer advised the hard rubbish will definitely be provided for within this financial year and noted that the Shire understands that the usual timeframe of services did not happen, however services paid for in rates will happen just not in the same time.

RESOLUTION NUMBER:C-8-8-2026
OFFICER RECOMMENDATION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Mehta
Seconded by:Cr Daw
That Council resolves to approve the development application for the proposed Tourist and Visitor Accommodation at Lot 73 (No.310) Hopedale Rise, Wooroloo, subject to the following conditions:
  1. This planning approval is only for Tourist and Visitor Accommodation as defined by Local Planning Scheme No. 4 and shown on the approved plans.
  2. The development must comply with the approved plans (including any amendments marked in red) unless approval is granted by the Shire for any minor variation made necessary by detailed design.
  3. Prior to commencement of operation, the development must be connected to the approved on-site effluent disposal system which has been installed to the satisfaction of the Shire's Health Service.
  4. Prior to commencement of operation, information is to be provided to demonstrate that the measures contained in Section 6.1; 6.2 Responsibilities for implementation and Management of the Required Bushfire Measures as set out under the Bushfire Management Plan dated 20 March 2026 have been implemented to the satisfaction of the Shire. This information should include a completed 'Certification by Bushfire Consultant' from the bushfire management plan. 
  5. For the duration of development, the landowner(s)/occupier(s) must ensure compliance with the approved Bushfire Emergency Evacuation Plan. This includes, but is not limited to the following:
    1. An up-to-date copy of the Emergency Evacuation Plan being always made available.
    2. A copy of the Emergency Evacuation Plan Notice being displayed on site in visible locations throughout the building.
    3. Signage and signposting (where appropriate) to provide users with wayfinding during times of emergency.
    4. Closure of the development when the Fire Danger Index reaches 75 being an extreme or catastrophic rating
  6. Prior to commencement of operation, an updated Bushfire Emergency Evacuation Plan must be submitted to and approved by the Shire of Mundaring.
  7. All stormwater must be managed onsite to prevent erosion and transportation of water borne pollutants, to the satisfaction of the Shire.
  8. All native vegetation on the lot must be retained unless clearing is specifically exempt under the Local Planning Scheme No 4 or required under an approved Bushfire Management Plan. 
  9. The approved Operational Management Plan must be implemented for the duration of the development to the satisfaction of the Shire of Mundaring.
  10. A maximum of two (2) tents are permitted under this approval, with a maximum occupancy of two (2) adults per tent and should the landowner(s) wish to increase the number, an amended development application must be submitted to the Shire for approval.
  11. All parking associated with the development must be contained on site and in the approved location at all times.
  12. Prior to commencement of operation, all car parking areas must meet the following requirements:
    1. The provision and maintenance of a minimum of two (2) car parking spaces, which are designed, constructed, sealed, kerbed, drained, and marked in accordance with Australian/New Zealand Standard AS/NZS 2890.1:2004, Parking facilities, Part 1: Off street car parking and in addition to the above;
    2. The provision and maintenance of one (1) car parking space(s) dedicated to people with disabilities, which are designed, constructed, sealed, kerbed, drained and marked in accordance with Australian/New Zealand Standard AS/NZS 2890.6:2009, Parking facilities, Part 6: Off street parking for people with disabilities and which are linked to the main entrance of the development by a continuous accessible path of travel designed and constructed in accordance with Australian Standard AS 1428.1 2009, Design for access and mobility, Part 1: General requirements for access New building work.

CARRIED 9/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Grills, Cr Cicchini, Cr Woods, Cr Strutt
Against:None

Moved by:Cr Mehta

That Council:
  1. Supports the Mundaring Music Muster 2027 under the Arts Culture and Events Funding Program, subject to the applicant providing: 
    • Detailed event management and operational plans, including risk management plan, traffic management plan, emergency management plan, waste management plan, accessibility and inclusion plan;
    • Confirmation of suitable headlining artists contacts;
    • Confirmation of sponsorship and income sources.
  2. Approve funding of $100,000 (Year 1) to UFX Event Engineers Pty Ltd under the Tier 1 – Signature Event, subject to the event being held in March/April or May.
  3. Require standard funding agreement conditions, including: 
    • Acknowledgement of the Shire’s support in all promotional materials;
    • Post-event reporting on attendance and economic outcomes; and
  4. Notes the applicant's request for a multi-year funding arrangement. RESOLUTION NUMBER:C-10-8-2026 
MOTION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Pres McNeil
Seconded by:Cr Mehta
That Council:
  1. Supports the Mundaring Music Muster 2027 under the Arts Culture and Events Funding Program, subject to the applicant providing: 
    • Detailed event management and operational plans, including risk management plan, traffic management plan, emergency management plan, waste management plan, accessibility and inclusion plan;
    • Confirmation of suitable headlining artists contacts;
    • Confirmation of sponsorship and income sources.
  2. Approve funding of $85,000 (Year 1) to UFX Event Engineers Pty Ltd under the Tier 1 – Signature Event, subject to the event being held in March/April or May.
  3. Require standard funding agreement conditions, including: 
    • Acknowledgement of the Shire’s support in all promotional materials;
    • Post-event reporting on attendance and economic outcomes; and
  4. Notes the applicant's request for a multi-year funding arrangement. Subject to successful delivery of the 2027 event, achievement of agreed attendance and economic outcomes, and satisfactory acquittal of funding, Council may consider a future multi-year funding agreement through a subsequent report.

CARRIED 5/4
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Ellery, Cr Grills, Cr Woods
Against:Cr Daw, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Cicchini, Cr Strutt

Reason for Change:
The proposed three-day event is expected to attract more than 10,000 people and was originally proposed to be held in January, during a period of heightened bushfire risk in the Perth Hills. Given the scale of the event and its location within a bushfire-prone area, holding the event in March, April or May is considered a prudent risk-management measure that would reduce the potential emergency evacuation, traffic management and public safety risks associated with hosting a large-scale event during peak bushfire season. The funding amount has also been reduced from $100,000 to $85,000 to retain capacity within the Arts, Culture and Events Funding Program budget to support additional events during the current financial year, while still providing substantial financial support for the proposed signature event.

MOTION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Cicchini
Seconded by:Cr Woods
That Council, by Absolute Majority, resolves to:
  1. Amend proposed clause 2.24(5) of the Activities on Thoroughfares and Trading in Thoroughfares and Public Places Amendment Local Law 2026 (Attachment 1) and clause 4.11 of the Local Government Property Local Law Amendment Local Law (Attachment 2) by deleting the words "within 2 days after the close of polling" and replacing them with "within 7 days after the close of polling;
  2. Pursuant to section 3.12(3) of the Local Government Act 1995, approve for public consultation the proposed:
    1. Shire of Mundaring Local Government Property Amendment Local Law 2026; and
    2. Shire of Mundaring Activities on Thoroughfares and Trading in Thoroughfares and Public Places Amendment Local Law 2026.
  3. Authorise the Chief Executive Officer to: 
    1. Give local public notice of the proposed amendment local laws in accordance with section 3.12(3)(a) of the Local Government Act 1995;
    2. Make copies of the proposed amendment local laws available for inspection and copying by the public in accordance with section 3.12(3)(b) of the Local Government Act 1995; 
    3. Invite submissions in relation to the proposed amendment local laws for a period of not less than 42 days after publication of the public notice in accordance with section 3.12(3)(c) of the Local Government Act 1995;
    4. Submit copies of the proposed amendment local laws and public notice to the Minister for Local Government in accordance with section 3.12(3)(d) of the Local Government Act 1995; and 
    5. Undertake all administrative actions necessary to progress the statutory local law-making process.
  1. Receive a further report following the public consultation period detailing:
    1. Submissions received;
    2. Any recommended amendments arising from submissions; and
    3. The proposed adoption of the amendment local laws.

BY ABSOLUTE MAJORITY CARRIED 9/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Grills, Cr Cicchini, Cr Woods, Cr Strutt
Against:None

Reason for Change:
The proposed local laws introduce a requirement for election signs to be removed within two days of the close of polling. Council's existing Policy 2.26 Temporary Election Signage allows a seven-day removal period. Aligning the local law with the existing policy framework will provide consistency for candidates, simplify administration and enforcement, and reflect Council's previously adopted policy position. Moved by:Cr Cicchini

  1. That Council adopt the revised Terms of Reference for the Australia Day Citizenship Awards Committee (Attachment 1), subject to the following amendments to 4.1:
  • Junior Citizen of the Year– (up to 15 years) Young people (individual or group) who, through their volunteering activities, have made a meaningful contribution to the local community; 
  • Access Mundaring – recognises an individual or group, who, through their volunteering efforts, makes a difference to create a more accessible and inclusive local community; and
  • Volunteer Capacity
    For the purposes of these awards, a volunteer is a person who freely contributes their time, skills or expertise for community benefit. Receiving a nominal allowance, reimbursement of expenses, stipend, sitting fee or honorarium that is not intended as salary or commercial remuneration, does not exclude a nominee from being considered a volunteer.
  1. That Council, by absolute majority, appoints the Shire President to the Australia Day Citizenship Awards Committee.

BY ABSOLUTE MAJORITY CARRIED 9/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Grills, Cr Cicchini, Cr Woods, Cr Strutt
Against:None

Reason for Change
To give clarity that volunteers who receive a nominal allowance, reimbursement of expenses, stipend, sitting fee or honorarium, are still eligible for nomination. That the Australia Day Citizenship Awards are focussed on volunteering, rather than wage earners from their roles.

06:32 pm – Point of Order
Cr Mehta raised a point of order in accordance with the Shire of Mundaring Meeting Procedure Local Law 2015, section 7.2(1)(a), on the basis that Cr Grills’ remarks were not relevant to the matter under discussion and were not being presented as a concise question. After hearing the point of order, Pres McNeil directed Cr Grills to keep his question succinct. The point of order was upheld.

06:47 pm – Point of Order
Cr Grills raised a point of order during debate, advising that he had not stated that councillors should be involved in the recruitment process. After considering the point of order, Pres McNeil acknowledged that this had not been stated and ruled accordingly. The point of order was upheld.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Environmental Funding Success
I'm pleased to share that the Shire has secured $150,000 in funding through the Western Australian Government's Community Stewardship Grants program to support coordinated fox management across several important bushland reserves throughout our Shire. The project will help protect native wildlife, strengthen biodiversity outcomes and support long-term environmental stewardship in areas including Lake Leschenaultia and a number of our conservation reserves. I'd like to acknowledge our Environment and Sustainability team for their successful grant application and thank the Western Australian Government and DPIRD for their support of this important work. 
 
Tarmac West Rally
A reminder to residents that the Tarmac West Rally will return to the Perth Hills on Friday 18 September. Summary of QuestionsSummary of Response
Mariette Tanneau
1The Shire of Mundaring wishes to enforce sea container policies on us and cannot confirm when the policy will be applied on other community members. Policies should be enforced consistently to ensure fairness and compliance with regulations and be enforced on all individuals. When will the Shire confirm this, in writing, if and when they will apply the same policies on all community members in the Shire of Mundaring?The CEO advised in relation to the sea containers, the Shire does not actively seek out non-compliances, however if the Shire is made aware of a non-compliance or a sea container that is in an area it shouldn't be, then the Shire will take action. In response to how the Shire approaches equity, the CEO advised the Shire looks to ensure the application of Council policy and planning framework in an equitable manner. Again, the point and some of your frustration, results from the fact that the Shire won't proactively go out and look for those issues on non-compliance. However, if people do make a complaint, then the Shire will act.
2We have asked the Shire to investigate and inform us if the Leach drains at number 6 are renewed, if they are approved, if they are the correct distance to boundary, and if the distance to the winter creek is correctly applied. Landgate map viewer shows the distance between the leech drains and the winter creek is approximately 18 metres, and it should be at least 30 metres, which is why we have a native system. We would like to know, in writing, what investigation is being done and if the system is approved so we can confirm that the issues we are experiencing on our property are not coming from the neighbour's leech drains?The CEO advised that the response to the question around drainage and ground water is that Shire staff have investigated the concerns through site inspections and a review of the property records. Based on those investigations, the officers found no evidence linking the seepage to drainage infrastructure, waste disposal systems or other structure on the neighbouring property. 

The CEO advised he has already provided a response via email, however there were additional information points referenced that he hasn't been privy to and asked for those details to be sent to him to enable the formulation of a more detailed response.
Eric Smith
1What is the total amount of purchases of vehicles and equipment for the 2025/2026 financial year for the Shire of Mundaring?The CEO advised that in the Shire's monthly financial reports is a list of plant replacement which is provided to Council every month. Question taken on notice to provide further detail.
2What is the total cost of income from trade-ins and sales of vehicles and equipment for the financial year 2025/2026 for the Shire of Mundaring?The CEO advised that in the Shire's monthly financial reports is a list of plant replacement which is provided to Council every month. The CEO advised the question will be taken on notice to provide further detail.
3What is or has been the control of corporate cards and has there been a reduction in user use and cost and has there been a reduction in the number or corporate cards in use?The CEO advised that he was not aware of a reduction in corporate cards. There are strong internal controls in place to make sure that expenditure going onto the cards is appropriate and further to that Council is provided with a list of every item of expenditure that is incurred on credit cards as part of the accounts for payment which is presented at every monthly Council meeting. The community and council have oversight of all expenditure on credit cards.
4When is Council going to make safe many of the road edges? Many of these edges have worn/washed away from the weather causing up to several centimetres of drop from the bitumen edge. There are many roads throughout the Shire that require attention.The CEO advised the Shire takes every endeavour to make sure the Shire is maintaining our roads to a suitable standard. The Shire of Mundaring has a substantial road network, and the Shire is unable to be everywhere all the time. The CEO strongly encouraged the community, if there are issues found with the roads, to notify the Shire through our online customer request system, or over phone, or come into the Shire's front counter, to enable the Shire to investigate and take appropriate remedial action as required.
Justin Harris
1My question is regarding safety and parking along Homestead Road. Residents have concerns about public safely, lack of street lighting and parking along Homestead Road adjacent to the Mahogany Inn. What action is the Council taking to improve safety and address parking issues in this area and when can residents expect to see improvements?The Director Built and Natural Environment advised he had received the letter today from the Mahogany Creek Progress Association and also had the information forwarded to Cr. Mehta. The Shire acknowledges there is overflow parking that occurs from the Mahogany Inn and previous investigations have taken place and have addressed issues as appropriate under the parking local law. The Director Built and Natural Environment advised he will undertake further investigations and will provide a response once those investigations are complete.

Summary of Questions
Summary of Response
Kerry Stampfer
1Concerning the lower Hardey Road egress issue, can the council work with DWER who owns the land, and Western Power whose lines which run adjacent, and work out an emergency access way similar to the one that is between Darlington Road and Padbury Avenue Darlington?The Director of Built Environment advised he is aware of the matter and notes that Shire Officer Karen Dore is currently on leave and on her return, he will undertake further investigative discussions with Karen. He will then arrange a meeting on site with Karen Dore, Kerry, and one of the other neighbours. He advised that the issue of creating an additional egress is certainly problematic. 
2Concerning the new LPS, the properties along Hardey Road are not eligible for rezoning. However, Council's response is they will investigate if the subdivision is allowed. None of the properties around are up for rezoning so therefore how can the subdivision be allowed?The CEO advised this question will be taken on notice.
Mariette Tanneau
3
What is the role of council members, can we contact Council members when there are issues in working together with the Shire to find solutions to the issues we experience. I received an email from the Shire President, and I was asked not to copy in the Councillors to correspondence?
The CEO advised that he had already responded to this question via email the advice provided regarding ccíng Councillors into emails was not saying the members of the community could not Councillors, in fact it is encouraged, however in this instance the email was involving Councillors in operational questions and answers, which Councillors do not have a role in (according to legislation).
As additional information to the initial response provided the following had previously been provided to Mrs Tanneau.
There is an important distinction between the role of Councillors, the Council, the CEO and the administration. The ongoing discussions you are having with staff are operational in nature and, as such, Councillors are generally not included in these types of ongoing correspondence. This is because Councillors should avoid becoming involved in operational decision making. The advice you received was not suggesting that you should not contact Councillors. Rather, it was indicating that ongoing discussions regarding approvals and operational matters are best managed through the administration. As referenced previously, if you have a complaint, we encourage you to make this formally through the Shire's complaint process. If you wish to alert Councillors to a matter, you are also welcome to do so, and Councillors may then raise the matter with the CEO as appropriate.

OFFICER RECOMMENDATION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Mehta
Seconded by:Cr Strutt
That Council by Absolute Majority:
  1. Receives the report regarding the review of the Shire of Mundaring Health Local Law 2003.
  2. Notes that the existing Health Local Law is subject to the transitional review provisions contained within clause 65 of Schedule 9.3 of the Local Government Act 1995 and must be reviewed prior to 7 December 2026.
  3. Determines, subject to consideration of community submissions, that the preferred outcome of the review is to:
    1. Repeal the Shire of Mundaring Health Local Law 2003; and
    2. Adopt a replacement Health Local Law 2026 under the Local Government Act 1995.
  4. Approves the proposed replacement Local Law for public consultation in accordance with sections 3.12 and 3.16 of the Local Government Act 1995.
  5. Authorises the Chief Executive Officer to:
    1. Publish statewide and local public notices of the proposed local law;
    2. Invite submissions for a minimum period of six weeks; and
    3. Undertake all actions necessary to facilitate the statutory consultation process.
  6. Requests a further report be presented to Council following the public consultation period outlining submissions received and recommending whether the proposed replacement local law should proceed to gazettal.

BY ABSOLUTE MAJORITY CARRIED 9/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Grills, Cr Cicchini, Cr Woods, Cr Strutt
Against:None

That Cr Mehta be allowed a three-minute extension of time to speak to this item, in accordance with clause 6.11 of the Shire of Mundaring Meeting Procedures Local Law 2015.
CARRIED 9/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Grills, Cr Cicchini, Cr Woods, Cr Strutt
Against:None

REASONS
Proposing an amendment to recognise the Local Governments bushfire mitigation work.
 
SUBSTANTIVE MOTION  
Moved by:Cr Mehta
Seconded by:Cr Strutt
That Council requests that the Western Australian Local Government Association develop a formal policy and advocacy position on insurance affordability and resilience‑based insurance frameworks for the WA local government sector, with particular regard to:
  1. recognition of household bushfire mitigation measures in insurance pricing;
  2. recognition of Local Governments bushfire‑mitigation work, including fuel management, resilient local infrastructure and emergency preparedness, in how insurers assess local risk and set premiums;
  3. improved transparency regarding mitigation actions that may reduce insurance premiums and excesses; and
  4. the implications of rising insurance costs for community resilience and under-insurance in bushfire-prone areas. 

OFFICER COMMENTS

ALTERNATIVE MOTION   

Moved by:Cr Ellery

That Council, in accordance with Schedule 2, Part 4, Clause 20(2) of the Planning and Development (Local Planning Schemes) Regulations 2015, recommends that the Western Australian Planning Commission approves proposed Structure Plan 83 (refer Attachment 1) subject to the following modifications: 

PART A
  1. Modification of the Bushfire Management Plan (BMP) in accordance with the advice received from the Department of Fire and Emergency Services (DFES), to address the following matters to the satisfaction of DFES and Shire of Mundaring:
    1. Element 3 - Vehicular Access; and (including access to Katherine Street)
  2. Modification of the Transport Impact Assessment (TIA), in accordance with the advice of Main Roads Western Australia (MRWA), to address the following matters to the satisfaction of MRWA, Shire of Mundaring and City of Swan:
    1. To further investigate the capacity of the regional road network and surrounding intersections and identify any road or intersection upgrades required to accommodate projected growth associated with the development, including arrangements for the delivery of those upgrades to ensure the transport network can adequately accommodate the project population growth within the locality; and
  3. Modification of the Structure Plan Report and Map, to the satisfaction of the Shire of Mundaring, MRWA and Perth Airport: 
    1. To reflect the findings and recommendations of the finalised TIA and associated technical note(s); and
    2. In accordance with the advice received from the Department of Transport and Major Infrastructure (DTM), to include notations identifying future/ indicative connections for pedestrians and active transport users to:
      1. The Roe Highway Principal Shared Path (PSP) along the western boundary of the site; and
      2. Clayton Street, aligned with Henkin Street and/or Pascoe Street; and
    3. To show and address the current ANEF (2026) contours; and
    4. In accordance with the revised proposal presented to and considered by Perth Airport, in their submission dated 19 June 2026, and State Planning Policy 5.1 - Land Use Planning in the Vicinity of Perth Aiport, to include: 
      1. Removal of the proposed R30/R40 density coding; and
      2. Application of a residential density coding no greater than R25 across the Structure Plan area; and 
      3. Inclusion of a provision stating that, notwithstanding the R25 density coding, the minimum lot size across the Structure Plan area (excluding the Local Centre) shall be no less than the minimum lot size applicable to Residential R20 development under the Residential Design Codes, with no variations or concessions applying; and 
      4. Inclusion of a provision stating a maximum dwelling yield of 400 dwellings across the Structure Plan area, with no variations or concessions applying; and
    5. To demonstrate all road reserves within the Structure Plan area are no less than 16 metres in width to facilitate new street tree planting in accordance with the Shire's Street Trees Local Planning Policy (PS-08); and
    6. Part 1, Section 3.1 to include section titled 'Consultation with the City of Swan' to read: Subdivision applications proposing: (a) a new connection to Wilkins Street; (b) a new connection to Henkin Street; or (c) upgrades to the Wilkins Street/ Henkin Street intersection, are to be referred to the City of Swan as a road authority, prior to determination; and
    7. To address inconsistencies in relation to Public Open Space (POS) and ensure the final layout demonstrates that the credited POS is delivered in accordance with Liveable Neighbourhoods.
  4. Council Requests the WAPC seek further advice from DWER if a revised District Water Management Strategy or Foreshore Management Plan should be required in assessing SP83 in accordance with SPP2.9.
PART B
  1. Council requests the Chief Executive Officer to provide Council with an briefing at the November Forum on the status of relevant WAPC subdivision conditions applying to the Robinson Grove Phase 1 area relating to foreshore management and works, based on information available from the relevant State Government agencies.
  2. Council requests the CEO write to the developer encouraging them to collaborate with Bibbul Ngarma Aboriginal Association's Mandoon Bilya parkland regarding associated foreshore works and adjacent POS.

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Rates Prize Draw  
I’m excited to share that our eRates promotion has once again received a positive response from the community. All ratepayers who registered and were subscribed to eRates by the rates due date were automatically entered into today’s prize draw.\u202F 
\u202F 
We have eight prizes to draw, with each winner receiving a $500 credit towards their rates assessment. If a winner has already paid their rates in full or in part, any remaining credit will be refunded after the $500 credit has been applied.\u202F 
\u202F 
It’s also encouraging to see more members of our community choosing to receive their rates notices electronically. eRates subscriptions have grown from 3,338 in September 2025 to 3,605 in September 2026, an increase of 267 subscribers, or approximately 8.0 per cent.\u202F 
\u202F 
This continued growth reflects our community’s increasing acceptance of electronic rates notices and helps support a more convenient and efficient way of communicating with ratepayers.\u202F 
Current Council Members and Shire employees are not eligible to enter.\u202F 
\u202F 
I’d like to ask Cr Ellery, Deputy Shire President to draw our eight prize winners. Good luck to everyone in the draw.\u202F Winners of the Rates Prize Draw were:

  • Yankuang Resources Pty Ltd  
  • Serenitas Communities Holdings Pty Ltd  
  • JR and KL Middleton 
  • Heart N Soul Health & Fitness Pty Ltd 
  • DC & LP Brajkovich 
  • BS & JF Perry 
  • BA & LN Jenkins 
  • GA & JA Woods 

Future Mundaring 
I’m very pleased to share that we’ve officially launched Future Mundaring, a new long-term conversation with our community about the future of the places we call home. 
 
Over the coming years, there are some important conversations ahead about how our communities grow and change. Future Mundaring will bring those conversations together and give residents a clearer and more connected way to get involved. 
 
The first step is a series of community workshops being held across the Shire this month, where we’re asking people what they value about their communities, what they would like to see improved and what they want for the future. What we hear through these conversations will help inform our Place Plans and future decision-making. 
 
Every part of our Shire has its own character and priorities, so I strongly encourage residents across our Hills, Foothills and Rural communities to get involved and help us shape the future of the places we call home. 

Mundaring Cultural Hub 
I’m also pleased to acknowledge another important milestone for the Mundaring Cultural Hub, with the project progressing to the tender stage. 
 
This is an exciting step forward, not only for the Cultural Hub itself, but for the wider revitalisation of the Mundaring town centre. 
 
The Cultural Hub will be an important catalyst for that transformation, helping create a more vibrant and welcoming town centre and a place that brings people together through community, culture and creativity. 
 
It’s a significant investment in the future of Mundaring, and I’m excited to see this project continue moving from planning towards delivery. 
 
Chidlow RV Rest Stop 
It’s also great to see the Chidlow RV Rest Stop moving towards completion. 
 
Located in the heart of Chidlow, the facility will provide dedicated overnight parking for self-contained recreational vehicles, along with a wastewater dump point and supporting infrastructure. 
 
The project is about encouraging more visitors to stop, stay and explore Chidlow and the wider Perth Hills, creating more opportunities for our local businesses and supporting our visitor economy. 
 
I’d also like to acknowledge the State Government’s $100,000 contribution towards the project and the community feedback that helped shape its location. 
 
2027 Citizenship Awards 
Finally, nominations are now open for the 2027 Shire of Mundaring Australia Day Citizenship Awards, and I’d encourage everyone to think about someone in our community who deserves to be recognised. 
 
Across our Shire there are people who quietly give their time, energy and care to help others, strengthen their communities and make the Perth Hills a wonderful place to live. 
 
This year there are five categories recognising young people, inspirational volunteers, contributions to accessibility and inclusion, and those who have dedicated many years to serving their community. 
 
If there’s someone who comes to mind, please take the time to nominate them. It’s a simple but meaningful way to say thank you and make sure the people who contribute so much to our community receive the recognition they deserve.

Summary of Questions
Summary of Response
Mark Richards - Bellevue Resident & Ratepayers Association
1Item 10.1 describes the proposal as up to 350 dwellings on page 158, but page 160 says the yield is capped at 400 and recommendation sets a maximum of 400. The structure plan advertised from 19 December 2025 capped yield at 350. Which figure applied to this advertised proposal and was the traffic assessment tested for 400 dwellings?Coordinator Strategic Planning advised that the application was advertised as about approximately 350 dwellings as is the applicant's intention with the site.  The cap of 400 is suggested to balance the considerations of the State Planning Policies to allow for more detailed design at the subdivision stage should there be the need to go up to that 400, however, the applicant's intention at this stage is the 350.

Director Place & Community advised, with regards to the traffic impact assessment undertaken, the assessment was undertaken on 345 dwellings, but it also factored in a higher density yield, so assumed plus 15, so it was done on 360.
2Did the transport impact assessment or technical note 1(a) include traffic from Structure Plan 80, and if not, will this be addressed under modification 2?Director Built & Natural Environment advised that the traffic impact study would have included all the lot yield up until this current structure plan.
Eric Smith - Glen Forrest
1When is the railway sign going to be brought back to its original full historic significance or has the other materials that should be there with it been used for other purposes or gone to scrap?This question was taken on notice.
2What progress has been done to correct the edges of many roads around the Shire?Director Built & Natural Environment advised that the Shire would require a list of the particular locations referred to by Mr Smith as the Shire also has a program of maintenance work, so are unable to be everywhere at all times.  If Mr Smith becomes aware of any particular locations he is encouraged to advise the Shire and those locations can be added to the programs.

The CEO further clarified that the Shire does have a program of works that it undertakes with respect to general maintenance on roads, which includes shoulders.  If Mr Smith has any areas of particular concern please advise the Shire and then it can be confirmed if those areas are on the program and if not, they can be added.
Lenn Barrett - Sawyers Valley
1In 2024 I received a transportable from Northern Eureka and ever since then I've asked the desk to please explain why it is still classed as a vacant block?  The CEO advised that as the Shire has Mr Barrett's address he will investigate why the property is still considered vacant land and will then reach out to Mr Barrell tomorrow or Thursday to provide some advice with respect to why it's remained as vacant land and if there is something that is required to be done to remove it from the vacant land list.
Eric Smith - Glen Forrest
3We have just passed the school holidays, why is the Bilgoman Aquatic Centre closed and when is the pool going to open?Director Place & Community advised that the Bilgoman Aquatic Centre will be opening on Saturday 24 October 2026.
4The Mundaring Shire or someone within the Shire made an arbitrary decision to relocate the Ford Blitz fire unit that used to belong to the Glen Forest Fire Brigade elsewhere and without no consultation when it should have been left and built and displayed within the Shire.  Why is it not keptwithin the Shire?
 
Director Built & Natural Environment advised that the Shire had contemplated what to do with the Blitz for quite some time and has spoke with the volunteer fire brigades through the Shire's Bush Fire Advisory Committee. The brigades have indicated that they were happy for the Shire to find a home that was prepared to look after it, which the Shire subsequently did,  through the Whiteman Park Museum where it is being well looked after and the brigade members are very happy with that outcome.

OFFICER RECOMMENDATION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Mehta
Seconded by:Cr Ellery
That Council: 
  1. Formally support permanent, publicly mapped Mining Avoidance Zones over all relevant ML1SA land within the Shire, including the Mundaring Weir Catchment and Northern Jarrah Forest  surrounding Mundaring and Sawyers Valley;
  2. Support protections which expressly prohibit all future exploration, investigative drilling, mining, mine pits, access roads and associated infrastructure, regardless of the proponent or mineral sought;
  3. Support the permanent excision of the protected land from ML1SA, together with any additional reservation, withdrawal or statutory protection necessary to prevent it becoming available to another mining company; and
  4. Provide written confirmation to Mr Adam Hort, MLA, Member of Kalamunda of the Shire’s position to be included in his representations to the Minister for State Development.

For:None
Against:None

 

RESOLUTION NUMBER:C-10-10-2026 
AMENDMENT / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Daw
Seconded by:Cr Ellery
That point 5 be added to the motion as follows:

  • That this matter of permanent mining avoidance zones be included in the Shire's Advocacy Strategy.

CARRIED 8/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Grills, Cr Woods, Cr Strutt
Against:None

RESOLUTION NUMBER: C-17-10-2026
OFFICER RECOMMENDATION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Mehta
Seconded by:Cr Ellery
That Council: 
  1. Adopts the revised Community Leases Policy 2.13 as attached, subject to;
    1. Rewording first sentence of 4.2.2 category one and category two to read - Incorporated associations and not-for-profit groups or organisations with a voluntary management committee and comprised mainly of local representatives;
    2. The addition of the following words at the end of 4.3.3 - Where the review identifies a potential change to the lease subsidy, any amendment will be subject to Council approval as part of the annual budget process and will not take effect until the relevant budget has been adopted;
    3. Replacing reference in the policy to rent reduction or adjustment with ‘Rent Relief’;
    4. The addition of the following words to 4.3.1 - Council may provide Rent Relief by way of a rent reduction, rent adjustment, funding offset, annual grant, or a combination of these measures;
    5. Adjusting 4.3.1 to reference - Rent Relief, funding offset or other form of financial assistance;
    6. The addition of the following words to 4.3.1 outlining when rent relief would be considered - Where Market Rent is applied to a Category Two leaseholder, Council may provide Rent Relief where the annual Market Rent exceeds 75% of the organisation's net operating result for the most recently completed financial year. For the purposes of this assessment, Council may consider the net operating result of the local operation, facility or service being conducted from the leased premises where this information is available and can be independently verified. Where the annual Market Rent exceeds 75% of the applicable net operating result, Council may apply a rent offset to the annual rent payable to an amount equal to 75% of the net operating result, or $10,000 per annum, whichever is the greater. Council retains discretion to determine the level and form of Rent Relief having regard to the organisation's financial circumstances, community benefit and strategic alignment with Council objectives.
    7. Remove from clause in 4.3.1 "Applications for a rent reduction or adjustment must be submitted and determined prior to execution of the lease." 
  2. Notes that the policy incorporates the outcomes of the Governance Workshop held on 18 August 2026, including the adoption of a financial sustainability adjustment mechanism for Category Two community leases.
CARRIED 8/0

RESOLUTION NUMBER: C-19-10-2026
OFFICER RECOMMENDATION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Ellery
Seconded by:Cr Mehta
That Council:
  1. Adopt the amended Policy 1.7 Designation of Senior Employees and Appointment of Acting or Temporary Chief Executive Officer as contained in Attachment 1, subject to:
    1. Amending clause 4.1. "Temporary CEO appointed may include an external recruitment process in accordance with the principles of merit and equity prescribed in section 5.40 of the Act."
  2. Remove Clause 4.1 Designation of Senior Employees from Policy 1.7, with the effect that the Chief Executive Officer remains the only Senior Employee of Council; and
  3. Authorise the Chief Executive Officer to make consequential administrative amendments to Council Policies to ensure references to Senior Employees align with Council's governance arrangements and the requirements of the Local Government Act 1995.

CARRIED 8/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Grills, Cr Woods, Cr Strutt
Against:None

RESOLUTION NUMBER:C-23-10-2026 
OFFICER RECOMMENDATION / COUNCIL DECISION   
Moved by:Cr Ellery
Seconded by:Cr Mehta
That by Absolute Majority Council:
  1. Notes that the appraisal of Mr Jason Whitetaker, Chief Executive Officer, has been completed for the period of July 2025 to June 2026 and his performance was deemed to have met the performance requirements of the position of CEO to a high level during the review period.
  2. Endorses by absolute majority the findings of the Summary Report as presented by Price Consulting and thanks Mr Whiteaker for his efforts.
  3. Approves an increase of 3.79% to Mr Whiteaker’s salary (cash component) and 3.89% on TRP effective 1 July 2026; and 
  4. Approves the CEO’s Performance Criteria for the 2026-2027 period, as per Confidential Attachment 1.

CARRIED BY ABSOLUTE MAJORITY 8/0
For:Pres McNeil, Cr Mehta, Cr Daw, Cr Ellery, Cr Heptinstall, Cr Grills, Cr Woods, Cr Strutt
Against:None

Annual Electors Meeting 2025

Tuesday, February 4, 2025 - 06:30 PM

Shire of Mundaring will hold the Annual Electors’ Meeting on Tuesday, 4 February 2025, commencing at 6.30pm in the Council Chamber, 7000 Great Eastern Highway, Mundaring.

The purpose of the meeting is to:

1. Adopt the 2023/24 Annual Report; and
2. General Business

The 2023/24 Annual Report can be found on the Shire of Mundaring website Annual Reports and Progress Reporting » Shire of Mundaring with hardcopies available to view at the Mundaring Shire Administration Centre and Mundaring and Boya Public Libraries.

The General Business section of the meeting provides electors the opportunity to ask questions or submit motions for consideration by Council. I encourage representatives of Community Associations to attend and raise ideas or priorities on behalf of your community members.

View the Electors Meeting Guidelines outline to learn how the meeting will proceed.

Please note that priority will be given to questions and motions received at least two business days prior to the meeting. Additional questions and motions presented at the meeting may be considered, if time permits.

To submit a question or motion, please email the completed form to shire@mundaring.wa.gov.au by 4pm, Thursday 30 January 2025.

Council value our community’s participation and we look forward to a respectful and productive exchange of new ideas, focus areas and opportunities for improvement

Please note, this meeting will be audio recorded and livestreamed.

Page Title

Special Council Meeting 2 May 2023

Tuesday, May 2, 2023 - 6:30 PM

Location

Council Chamber, Shire of Mundaring Administration Building, 7000 Great Eastern Highway, Mundaring

A special meeting of Council will be held on Tuesday, 2 May 2023 commencing at 6.30pm.

The purpose of this meeting is to consider the Shire’s referral response to the WA Planning Commission’s (WAPC) reconsideration of Structure Plan 34 – North Stoneville (SP34).
